title.zh: 卷九十一 列傳第十六 溫皇甫二李姜崔
title.en: Volume 91 Biographies 16: Wen, Huang, Fu, Er, Li, Jiang, Cui
title.raw: 卷九十一 列傳第十六 溫皇甫二李姜崔 Volume 91 Biographies 16: Wen, Huang, Fu, Er, Li, Jiang, Cui

sentences.zh: 溫皇甫二李姜崔

translations.literal: Wen, Huangfu, the two Lis, Jiang, and Cui.
translations.idiomatic: Biographies of the Wen, Huangfu, two Li, Jiang, and Cui families.

sentences.zh: 溫大雅，字彥弘，并州祁人。

translations.literal: Wen Daya, courtesy name Yanhong, was a man of Qi in Bingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Daya, whose courtesy name was Yanhong, came from Qi in Bingzhou.

sentences.zh: 父君攸，北齊文林館學士，入隋為泗州司馬，

translations.literal: His father Junyou was a scholar of the Northern Qi Wenlin Academy; entering the Sui, he served as marshal of Sizhou.
translations.idiomatic: His father Junyou had been a scholar in the Northern Qi's Wenlin Academy and later served the Sui as marshal of Sizhou.

sentences.zh: 見朝政不綱，謝病歸。

translations.literal: Seeing that court governance lacked discipline, he resigned citing illness and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: When he saw that the court had lost its discipline, he pleaded illness and withdrew to his home.

sentences.zh: 大雅性至孝，與弟彥博、大有皆知名，薛道衡見之，嘆曰：「三人者，皆卿相才也。」

translations.literal: Daya was by nature profoundly filial; he and his younger brothers Yanbo and Dayou were all well known. When Xue Daoheng saw them, he sighed and said, "These three men all have the talent of chief ministers and grand councillors.
translations.idiomatic: Daya was deeply filial by nature. He and his younger brothers Yanbo and Dayou were all celebrated, and when Xue Daoheng met them he exclaimed, "All three of these men possess the makings of chief ministers.

sentences.zh: 初為東宮學士、長安尉，以父喪解，會天下亂，不復仕。

translations.literal: At first he served as a scholar in the Eastern Palace and as magistrate of Chang'an, but left office on his father's death; as the empire fell into chaos, he never took office again.
translations.idiomatic: He had first served as a scholar in the crown prince's palace and as magistrate of Chang'an, but left office to mourn his father; with the realm in turmoil, he never returned to public service.

sentences.zh: 彥博字大臨，通書記，警悟而辯。

translations.literal: Yanbo, courtesy name Dalin, was versed in documentary writing, alert and eloquent in debate.
translations.idiomatic: Yanbo, whose courtesy name was Dalin, mastered documentary writing and was quick-witted and sharp in debate.

sentences.zh: 開皇末，對策高策，授文林郎，直內史省。

translations.literal: At the end of the Kaihuang era, in the policy examination he ranked at the top of the high tier and was appointed Lang of the Forest of Literature, serving in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of Kaihuang he took the policy examination at the highest tier and was made a Lang of the Forest of Literature on duty in the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 隋亂，幽州總管羅藝引為司馬。

translations.literal: When the Sui fell into turmoil, Luo Yi, military governor of Youzhou, engaged him as marshal.
translations.idiomatic: As the Sui order collapsed, Luo Yi, military governor of Youzhou, brought him in as his marshal.

sentences.zh: 藝以州降，彥博與有謀，授總管府長史，封西河郡公。

translations.literal: When Yi surrendered the prefecture, Yanbo had shared in the planning; he was appointed chief administrator of the governorate headquarters and enfeoffed as Duke of Xihe.
translations.idiomatic: When Yi surrendered his prefecture, Yanbo had taken part in the plan; he was made chief administrator of the governorate headquarters and enfeoffed as Duke of Xihe.

sentences.zh: 召入為中書舍人，遷侍郎。

translations.literal: He was summoned to court as Attendant of the Secretariat and later promoted to Vice Minister.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to serve as an attendant of the Secretariat and later promoted to vice minister.

sentences.zh: 高麗貢方物，高祖欲讓而不臣，彥博執不可，曰：「遼東本周箕子國，漢玄菟郡，不使北面，則四夷何所瞻仰？」

translations.literal: Koguryŏ presented tribute goods; Gaozu wished to decline them without treating Koguryŏ as a subject state, but Yanbo held firm that this could not be done, saying, "Liaodong was in Zhou the state of Jizi, and under Han the Xuantu commandery—if we do not make them face north in submission, what will the four barbarians have to look up to?
translations.idiomatic: When Koguryŏ sent tribute, Gaozu wanted to refuse it without accepting Koguryŏ as a subject, but Yanbo insisted this would not do, saying, "Liaodong was Jizi's state under Zhou and the Xuantu commandery under Han—if we do not require them to face north as subjects, what will the four quarters have to revere?

sentences.zh: 帝納而止。

translations.literal: The emperor accepted this and desisted.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor took his advice and dropped the idea.

sentences.zh: 突厥入寇，彥博以并州道行軍長史戰太谷，王師敗績，被執。

translations.literal: When the Turks raided, Yanbo as chief administrator on the Bingzhou campaign route fought at Taigu; the imperial army suffered defeat and he was taken captive.
translations.idiomatic: When the Turks invaded, Yanbo served as chief administrator on the Bingzhou campaign staff and fought at Taigu; the imperial forces were defeated and he was captured.

sentences.zh: 突厥知近臣，數問唐兵多少及國虛實，彥博不肯對，囚陰山苦寒地。

translations.literal: The Turks knew he was a close courtier and repeatedly asked how many Tang troops there were and whether the state was strong or weak; Yanbo refused to answer and was imprisoned in the bitter cold of the Yin Mountains.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing he was an intimate of the court, the Turks repeatedly pressed him on Tang troop strength and the empire's true condition; Yanbo would not reply and was held in the freezing wastes of the Yin Mountains.

sentences.zh: 太宗立，突厥歸款，得還。

translations.literal: When Taizong came to the throne, the Turks submitted in good faith and he was able to return.
translations.idiomatic: After Taizong's accession the Turks offered submission, and he was able to come home.

sentences.zh: 授雍州治中，尋檢校吏部侍郎。

translations.literal: He was appointed Administrator of Yongzhou and soon made Acting Vice Minister of the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He was made administrator of Yongzhou and soon afterward acting vice minister of personnel.

sentences.zh: 彥博欲汰擇士類，寡術不能厭眾，訟牒滿廷，時譏其煩碎。

translations.literal: Yanbo wished to sift and select the class of scholars, but lacked the method to satisfy the multitude; litigation documents filled the court, and at the time he was mocked for being finicky and trivial.
translations.idiomatic: Yanbo wanted to screen and refine the scholar-official class, but his methods could not satisfy everyone; lawsuits piled up in court, and contemporaries mocked his fussiness.

sentences.zh: 復為中書侍郎，遷御史大夫，檢校中書侍郎事。

translations.literal: He again served as Vice Minister of the Secretariat, was promoted to Censor-in-Chief, and acted in the affairs of the Vice Minister of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He returned to vice minister of the Secretariat, rose to censor-in-chief, and concurrently handled secretariat vice-minister duties.

sentences.zh: 貞觀四年，遷中書令，封虞國公。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Zhenguan he was promoted to Grand Councillor of the Secretariat and enfeoffed as Duke of Yuguo.
translations.idiomatic: In 630 he was promoted to grand councillor of the Secretariat and enfeoffed as Duke of Yuguo.

sentences.zh: 突厥降，詔議所以安邊者，彥博請如漢置降匈奴五原塞，以為捍蔽，與魏徵廷爭，徵不勝其辯，天子卒從之。

translations.literal: When the Turks submitted, an edict ordered discussion of how to secure the border; Yanbo asked that, as under Han with surrendered Xiongnu at the Wuyuan passes, they be settled as a defensive screen. He debated this in court with Wei Zheng, who could not overcome his eloquence, and the Son of Heaven ultimately followed Yanbo.
translations.idiomatic: After the Turks surrendered, the court was ordered to debate border security; Yanbo proposed settling them within the passes as the Han had done with surrendered Xiongnu at Wuyuan, to serve as a buffer. He argued the point against Wei Zheng in open court; Zheng could not best him in debate, and the emperor finally sided with Yanbo.

sentences.zh: 其後突利可汗弟結社謀反，帝始悔雲。

translations.literal: Later, Jieshe, younger brother of the Tuli khaghan, plotted rebellion, and only then did the emperor begin to regret it.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Jieshe, brother of the Tuli khaghan, rose in rebellion, the emperor came to regret the policy.

sentences.zh: 彥博善辭令，每問四方風俗，臚布誥命，若成誦然；

translations.literal: Yanbo was skilled in formal rhetoric; whenever customs of the four quarters were inquired about or edicts and proclamations were drafted and issued, it was as if they were already complete.
translations.idiomatic: Yanbo excelled at court rhetoric; whenever the customs of distant regions were discussed or edicts were drafted and promulgated, his words seemed already perfected.

sentences.zh: 進止詳華，人皆拭目觀。

translations.literal: His comings and goings were detailed and splendid; all wiped their eyes to watch.
translations.idiomatic: His bearing was meticulous and splendid, and everyone watched him with rapt attention.

sentences.zh: 高祖嘗宴近臣，遣秦王諭旨，既而顧左右曰：「何如溫彥博？」

translations.literal: Gaozu once feasted his close ministers and sent the Prince of Qin to convey his intent; then he turned to those beside him and said, "How does he compare with Wen Yanbo?
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu once entertained his intimate ministers and had the Prince of Qin deliver his message; then he looked to those around him and asked, "How does that compare with Wen Yanbo?

sentences.zh: 十年，遷尚書右僕射，明年卒，年六十三。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he was promoted to Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs; the next year he died, aged sixty-three.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year of the reign he was made right vice director of the Department of State Affairs; he died the following year at sixty-three.

sentences.zh: 彥博性周慎，既掌機務，謝賓客不通，進見必陳政事利害。

translations.literal: Yanbo was by nature thorough and cautious; once he held the reins of state affairs, he declined visitors and would not receive guests; on entering audience he always set forth the benefits and harms of government matters.
translations.idiomatic: Yanbo was thorough and cautious by nature. Once he held the levers of policy he shut his door to guests; whenever he came before the throne he laid out the gains and risks of each matter of state.

sentences.zh: 卒後，帝嘆曰：「彥博以憂國故，耗思殫神，我見其不逮再期矣，恨不許少閑以究其壽。」

translations.literal: After his death the emperor sighed and said, "Yanbo, because he worried over the state, exhausted his thoughts and spent his spirit—I saw that he would not reach two more seasons; I regret that I did not allow him a little leisure to complete his allotted years.
translations.idiomatic: After his death the emperor lamented, "Yanbo wore himself out worrying for the realm—I could see he would not live two more seasons, and I regret that I never gave him a little rest to see out his years.

sentences.zh: 家貧無正寢，殯別室，帝命有司為構寢。

translations.literal: His family was poor and had no proper sleeping hall; the coffin was placed in a side room, and the emperor ordered the relevant offices to build a hall for the bier.
translations.idiomatic: His household was so poor there was no proper hall for the bier; the coffin lay in a side room until the emperor ordered the authorities to build one.

sentences.zh: 贈特進，謚曰恭，陪葬昭陵。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made Special Advancement; his posthumous title was Gong, and he was buried with honor at Zhaoling.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously honored as Special Advancement, given the posthumous name Gong, and interred beside Zhaoling.

sentences.zh: 子振、挺。

translations.literal: His sons were Zhen and Ting.
translations.idiomatic: His sons were Zhen and Ting.

sentences.zh: 振歷太子舍人，居喪以毀卒。

translations.literal: Zhen served as Attendant of the Heir Apparent; in mourning he ruined his health and died.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen served as an attendant in the heir apparent's household and died from grief and self-mortification during mourning.

sentences.zh: 挺尚千金公主，官延州刺史。

translations.literal: Ting married Princess Qianjin and held office as prefect of Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Ting married Princess Qianjin and served as prefect of Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 彥博曾孫曦，尚涼國長公主。

translations.literal: Yanbo's great-grandson Xi married the Princess of Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Yanbo's great-grandson Xi married the Princess of Liang.

sentences.zh: 大有，字彥將。

translations.literal: Dayou, courtesy name Yanjiang.
translations.idiomatic: Dayou, whose courtesy name was Yanjiang.

sentences.zh: 隋仁壽中，李綱薦之，授羽林騎尉。

translations.literal: In the Renshou era of the Sui, Li Gang recommended him and he was appointed Cavalry Captain of the Imperial Forest.
translations.idiomatic: During Sui Renshou, Li Gang recommended him and he was made a cavalry captain of the imperial guard.

sentences.zh: 高祖舉兵，引為太原令。

translations.literal: When Gaozu raised his army, he brought Dayou in as magistrate of Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu took up arms, he appointed Dayou magistrate of Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 從秦王徇西河，將行，高祖曰：「士馬單少，要須經略，以君參軍事，事之濟否，卜是行也。」

translations.literal: Following the Prince of Qin in the campaign against Xihe, as they were about to depart Gaozu said, "Troops and horses are few and thin; strategy is essential—I appoint you to assist in military affairs; whether the affair succeeds or fails, take this campaign as the augury.
translations.idiomatic: When he followed the Prince of Qin against Xihe, Gaozu said before they marched, "Our forces are few—we need careful planning. I make you my military adviser; whether we succeed will be decided on this campaign.

sentences.zh: 西河下，攝大將軍府記室，與兄大雅同掌機近，不自安，請徙它職。

translations.literal: After Xihe fell, he acted as Recorder of the Grand General's headquarters; he and his elder brother Daya together held confidential duties close to power, felt ill at ease, and asked to be moved to another post.
translations.idiomatic: After Xihe surrendered he served as acting recorder on the prince's staff, sharing confidential duties with his brother Daya; uneasy at holding so much power beside his kin, he asked for another assignment.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「我虛心待卿，何所自疑？」

translations.literal: The emperor said, "I treat you with an open heart—what are you doubting in yourself?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "I receive you with an open heart—why doubt yourself?

sentences.zh: 武德初，累遷中書侍郎，封清河郡公。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Wude he was repeatedly promoted to Vice Minister of the Secretariat and enfeoffed as Duke of Qinghe.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Wude he rose through several posts to vice minister of the Secretariat and was enfeoffed as Duke of Qinghe.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈鴻臚卿，謚曰敬。

translations.literal: He died; posthumously he was made Minister of Ceremonies, posthumous title Jing.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously made minister of ceremonies with the posthumous name Jing.

sentences.zh: 初，顏氏、溫氏在隋最盛，思魯與大雅俱事東宮，湣楚、彥博同直內史省，遊秦、大有典校秘閣，顏以學業優，而溫以職位顯於唐雲。

translations.literal: In the beginning the Yan and Wen clans were at their height under the Sui: Silu and Daya both served the Eastern Palace; Minchu and Yanbo served together in the Secretariat; Youqin and Dayou oversaw the imperial library—so it was said that the Yans were superior in scholarship while the Wens were distinguished in office under Tang.
translations.idiomatic: At first the Yan and Wen families were the most prominent under the Sui: Silu and Daya both served the crown prince's household; Minchu and Yanbo shared duty in the Secretariat; Youqin and Dayou curated the imperial library—people said the Yans excelled in learning while the Wens won distinction in Tang office.

sentences.zh: 大雅四世孫佶，字輔國，以字行。

translations.literal: Daya's great-great-grandson Ji, courtesy name Fuguo, was known by his courtesy name.
translations.idiomatic: Daya's four-times grandson Ji, courtesy name Fuguo, went by his courtesy name in daily use.

sentences.zh: 安祿山亂，往見平原太守顏真卿，助為守計。

translations.literal: When the An Lushan rebellion broke out, he went to see Yan Zhenqing, prefect of Pingyuan, and helped devise plans for defense.
translations.idiomatic: During the An Lushan rebellion he sought out Yan Zhenqing, prefect of Pingyuan, and helped him plan the city's defense.

sentences.zh: 李光弼厚遇之。

translations.literal: Li Guangbi treated him with great favor.
translations.idiomatic: Li Guangbi treated him with marked esteem.

sentences.zh: 後居鄴，薛嵩薦之朝，授太常丞，一謝嵩即去，屏處郊野，世推其高節。

translations.literal: Later he lived at Ye; Xue Song recommended him to court and he was appointed Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices; after one farewell to Song he departed, withdrew to the countryside, and the age praised his lofty integrity.
translations.idiomatic: He later lived at Ye; Xue Song recommended him to court and he was made vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, but after a single leave-taking of Song he withdrew to the wilds, and the world admired his integrity.

sentences.zh: 子造。

translations.literal: His son was Zao.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Zao.

sentences.zh: 造，字簡輿，姿表瑰傑，性嗜書，然盛氣，少所降屈。

translations.literal: Zao, courtesy name Jianyu, had a magnificent and heroic bearing, loved books by nature, yet was overbearing in spirit and seldom bowed to others.
translations.idiomatic: Zao, courtesy name Jian-yu, was striking in appearance, devoted to books, but proud in temper and rarely willing to yield to anyone.

sentences.zh: 不喜為吏，隱王屋山，人號其居曰「處士墅」。

translations.literal: He disliked serving as an official, retired to Mount Wangwu, and people called his dwelling the "Recluse's Villa."
translations.idiomatic: Disliking office, he withdrew to Mount Wangwu, and people called his home the Recluse's Villa.

sentences.zh: 壽州刺史張建封聞其名，書幣招禮，造欣然曰：「可人也！」

translations.literal: Zhang Jianfeng, prefect of Shouzhou, heard his name and sent a letter with gifts to invite and honor him; Zao said with pleasure, "This is a man one can follow!
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jianfeng, prefect of Shouzhou, heard of him and sent letters and gifts to summon him; Zao said gladly, "Here is a man worth following!

sentences.zh: 往從之。

translations.literal: He went to join him.
translations.idiomatic: He went to join him.

sentences.zh: 建封雖咨謀，而不敢縻以職事。

translations.literal: Although Jianfeng consulted him, he did not dare to bind him with official duties.
translations.idiomatic: Jianfeng sought his counsel but never dared tie him down with formal office.

sentences.zh: 及節度徐州，造謝歸下邳，慨然有高世心。

translations.literal: When Jianfeng became military commissioner of Xuzhou, Zao took leave and returned to Xiapi, sighing with a mind to transcend the world.
translations.idiomatic: When Jianfeng took command of Xuzhou, Zao resigned and went back to Xiapi, moved by a desire to leave the world behind.

sentences.zh: 建封恐失造，因妻以兄子。

translations.literal: Jianfeng, fearing to lose Zao, therefore gave him his elder brother's son in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: Afraid of losing him, Jianfeng married him to his nephew.

sentences.zh: 時李希烈反，攻陷城邑，天下兵鎮陰相撼，逐主帥自立，德宗患之。

translations.literal: At that time Li Xilie rebelled, stormed and seized cities; military commissioners throughout the realm secretly undermined one another, drove out their commanders and set themselves up, and Dezong was troubled.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xilie had risen in rebellion and was seizing cities; across the empire military governors were quietly undermining one another, ousting their superiors and declaring themselves rulers, and Dezong was deeply worried.

sentences.zh: 以劉濟方納忠於朝，密詔建封擇縱橫士往說濟，佐其必。

translations.literal: Because Liu Ji was then offering loyalty to the court, a secret edict ordered Jianfeng to choose a strategist to go persuade Ji and help secure his resolve.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Ji was then showing loyalty to the court, and the emperor secretly ordered Jianfeng to choose a skilled persuader to win Ji over and strengthen his commitment.

sentences.zh: 建封強署造節度參謀，使幽州。

translations.literal: Jianfeng forcibly appointed Zao staff adviser on the military commission and sent him to Youzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Jianfeng pressed Zao into service as a commission staff adviser and sent him to Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 造與濟語未訖，濟俯伏流涕曰：「僻陋不知天子神聖，大臣盡忠，願率先諸侯效死節。」

translations.literal: Before Zao had finished speaking with Ji, Ji bowed prostrate, weeping, and said, "In my remote ignorance I did not know the Son of Heaven's sacredness or that the great ministers are wholly loyal—I wish to take the lead among the feudatories in offering my life for righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: Before Zao had finished speaking with him, Ji prostrated himself in tears and said, "Living in obscurity I failed to see the emperor's sacred virtue and his ministers' loyalty—I wish to lead the regional lords in dying for the throne.

sentences.zh: 造還，建封以聞，詔馳驲入奏。

translations.literal: Zao returned; Jianfeng reported it, and an edict ordered him to enter court by urgent relay.
translations.idiomatic: When Zao returned, Jianfeng reported the success and the emperor ordered him brought to court by express courier.

sentences.zh: 天子愛其才，問造家世及年，對曰：「臣五世祖大雅，外五世祖李勣，臣犬馬之齒三十有二。」

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven admired his talent and asked about Zao's family background and age; he replied, "Your servant's fifth-generation ancestor was Daya; on the maternal side the fifth-generation ancestor was Li Jing; your servant's years as a beast of burden are thirty-two.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor admired his ability and asked his lineage and age; he answered, "My fifth-generation ancestor was Daya; on my mother's side the fifth-generation ancestor was Li Jing; I am thirty-two years old.

sentences.zh: 帝奇之。

translations.literal: The emperor marveled at him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was struck with wonder.

sentences.zh: 將用為諫官，以語泄乃止。

translations.literal: He was about to be used as a remonstrating official, but because word leaked out the appointment was stopped.
translations.idiomatic: He was about to be made a remonstrance official, but the plan leaked and was dropped.

sentences.zh: 復去，隱東都。

translations.literal: He left again and retired to the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: He withdrew again and lived in seclusion in the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 烏重胤奏致幕府。

translations.literal: Wu Chongyin memorialized to bring him into his staff.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Chongyin petitioned to have him join his staff.

sentences.zh: 長慶初，以京兆司錄為太原幽鎮宣諭使，召見，辭曰：「臣，府縣吏也，不宜行，恐四方易朝廷。」

translations.literal: At the beginning of Changqing he was made Imperial Commissioner to proclaim and instruct the Taiyuan and Youzhou commands while serving as Registrar of the Capital Metropolitan Prefecture; summoned to audience, he declined, saying, "Your servant is a prefectural and county official—unsuited for this mission; I fear the four quarters will look lightly on the court.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Changqing, while serving as registrar of the metropolitan prefecture, he was appointed commissioner to instruct the Taiyuan and Youzhou commands. When summoned he declined, saying, "I am only a local official—unfit for such a mission; the regions may take the court lightly if I am sent.

sentences.zh: 穆宗曰：「朕東宮時聞劉總，比年上書請覲，使問行期，乃不報。

translations.literal: Muzong said, "When I was in the Eastern Palace I heard of Liu Zong; in recent years he has memorialized requesting an audience, and when envoys asked his travel date he still did not reply.
translations.idiomatic: Muzong said, "I heard of Liu Zong when I was crown prince. These past years he has asked to come to court, yet when we inquired when he would travel he never answered.

sentences.zh: 卿為我行喻意，毋多讓。」

translations.literal: Go convey my intent on my behalf—do not decline overmuch."
translations.idiomatic: Go speak my mind for me—and do not refuse again."

sentences.zh: 因賜緋衣。

translations.literal: He was therefore granted scarlet robes.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then bestowed scarlet court robes on him.

sentences.zh: 至范陽，總橐鞬郊迎。

translations.literal: When he reached Fanyang, Zong came out in full armor to welcome him at the suburbs.
translations.idiomatic: At Fanyang, Zong met him at the outskirts in full armor.

sentences.zh: 造為開示禍福，總懼，矍然若兵在頸，繇是籍所部九州入朝。

translations.literal: Zao explained to him the blessings and calamities involved; Zong was afraid, started as if weapons were at his neck, and thereby registered the nine prefectures under his command for submission to court.
translations.idiomatic: Zao laid out the rewards and risks; Zong was terrified, as if a blade were at his throat, and thereupon surrendered the nine prefectures under his command to the court.

sentences.zh: 還，遷殿中侍御史。

translations.literal: On his return he was promoted to Attending Censor within the Palace.
translations.idiomatic: After his return he was promoted to attending censor in the palace.

sentences.zh: 田弘正遇害，以起居舍人復宣慰鎮州行營。

translations.literal: When Tian Hongzheng was assassinated, as Recorder of the Emperor's Movements he again went to proclaim comfort to the Zhenzhou field headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: After Tian Hongzheng was murdered, he was sent again as recorder of the emperor's movements to comfort the Zhenzhou field command.

sentences.zh: 頃之，李景儉以酒得過宰相，造坐與飲，出為朗州刺史。

translations.literal: Before long, Li Jingjian offended the chief minister while drunk; Zao sat and drank with him and was sent out as prefect of Langzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Li Jingjian insulted the chief minister while drunk; Zao had shared the drinking and was demoted to prefect of Langzhou.

sentences.zh: 開後鄉渠百里，溉田二千頃，民獲其利，號「右史渠」。

translations.literal: He opened a canal at Houxiang a hundred li long, irrigating two thousand qing of fields; the people gained the benefit, and it was called the "Right Historian Canal."
translations.idiomatic: He opened a hundred-li canal at Houxiang that irrigated two thousand qing of farmland; the people prospered from it and called it the Right Historian Canal.

sentences.zh: 召授侍御史，知彈奏。

translations.literal: He was recalled and appointed Attending Censor, in charge of impeachment.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled as attending censor in charge of impeachments.

sentences.zh: 請復硃衣豸冠示外廡，不聽。

translations.literal: He requested restoration of scarlet robes and the xieguan hat to display authority in the outer corridors; the request was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: He asked that censors again wear scarlet robes and the xieguan hat in the outer halls as a mark of authority; the court refused.

sentences.zh: 夏州節度使李祐拜大金吾，違詔進馬，造正衙抨劾。

translations.literal: Li You, military commissioner of Xiazhou, on taking office as Grand Commandant of the Golden Chariots presented horses in violation of the edict; Zao impeached him in the main audience hall.
translations.idiomatic: When Li You of Xiazhou was appointed grand commandant of the golden chariots he presented horses contrary to edict; Zao denounced him in open court.

sentences.zh: 祐曰：』吾夜入蔡州擒吳元濟，未嘗心動，今日膽落於溫御史。」

translations.literal: You said, "When I entered Caizhou by night and captured Wu Yuanji, my heart never trembled; today my courage fails before Censor Wen."
translations.idiomatic: You said, "When I stormed Caizhou at night and took Wu Yuanji, I never flinched—but today my courage fails before Censor Wen."

sentences.zh: 遷左司郎中，知御史雜事，進中丞。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Director of the Left Department, handled miscellaneous censorate affairs, and advanced to Vice Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to director of the left department, took charge of censorate business, and rose to vice censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 大和二年，內昭德寺火，延禁中「野狐落」，野狐落者，宮人所居也，死者數百人。

translations.literal: In the second year of Dahe, fire broke out at the inner Zhaode Temple and spread to the "Wild Fox Hollow" within the forbidden precincts—the Wild Fox Hollow being where palace women dwelt—and several hundred died.
translations.idiomatic: In 828 fire broke out at the inner Zhaode Temple and spread to the Wild Fox Hollow in the inner palace, the women's quarters; several hundred people died.

sentences.zh: 是日，宰相、兩省官、京兆尹、中尉、樞密皆集日華門，督神策兵救火所及，獨御史府不至。

translations.literal: That day the chief ministers, officials of the two departments, the metropolitan prefect, the palace commandant, and the privy councilors all gathered at Rihua Gate, directing the Shence troops to fight the fire wherever it reached; only the Censorate did not arrive.
translations.idiomatic: That day the chief ministers, secretariat and chancellery officials, the metropolitan prefect, the palace commandant, and privy councilors all gathered at Rihua Gate to direct the Shence army against the blaze—only the Censorate was absent.

sentences.zh: 造自劾曰：「臺系賊，恐人緣以構奸，申警備，乃得入。

translations.literal: Zao impeached himself, saying, "The Censorate is tied to malfeasance; I feared people would use the occasion to plot treachery, reported and tightened security, and only then was able to enter.
translations.idiomatic: Zao submitted a self-impeachment, saying, "The Censorate is entangled with wrongdoers; I feared someone would exploit the chaos, so I posted extra guards before I could enter.

sentences.zh: 臣請入三十直，崔蠡、姚合二十直，自贖。」

translations.literal: Your servant requests thirty days' salary forfeited; Cui Li and Yao He twenty days each, by way of self-redemption.
translations.idiomatic: I ask to forfeit thirty days' salary; let Cui Li and Yao He forfeit twenty days each as my share of the penalty.

sentences.zh: 宰相劾造不待罪於朝，而自許輕比，不可聽。

translations.literal: The chief ministers impeached Zao for not awaiting judgment in court but setting his own light penalty—this could not be accepted.
translations.idiomatic: The chief ministers objected that Zao had not waited for court judgment but fixed his own lenient penalty, which could not be allowed.

sentences.zh: 有詔皆奪一月俸。

translations.literal: An edict ordered all to forfeit one month's salary.
translations.idiomatic: An edict stripped them all of one month's pay.

sentences.zh: 造性剛急，人或忤己，雖貴勢，亦以氣出其上。

translations.literal: Zao was by nature stern and quick-tempered; if anyone offended him, even men of rank and power, he would vent his spirit over them.
translations.idiomatic: Zao was harsh and quick-tempered; anyone who crossed him, however powerful, felt his wrath.

sentences.zh: 道遇左補闕李虞，恚不避，捕從者笞辱。

translations.literal: On the road he met Left Supplementation Censor Li Yu, who in anger did not yield; Zao seized Yu's attendants and had them flogged and humiliated.
translations.idiomatic: On the road he met the left supplementation censor Li Yu, who in anger refused to step aside; Zao seized Yu's attendants and had them beaten.

sentences.zh: 左拾遺舒元褒等建言：「故事，供奉官惟宰相外無屈避。

translations.literal: Left Reminder Shu Yuangao and others submitted advice: "By precedent, among palace attendants only the chief minister need not be yielded to.
translations.idiomatic: The left reminder Shu Yuangao and others memorialized, "By precedent only the chief minister is exempt from yielding to palace attendants.

sentences.zh: 造棄蔑典禮，無所畏，辱天子侍臣。

translations.literal: Zao has cast aside and despised canonical ritual, fears nothing, and insults the Son of Heaven's attending ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Zao has scorned court ritual, fears nothing, and humiliates the emperor's personal attendants.

sentences.zh: 凡事小而關分理者，不可失；

translations.literal: In all affairs, what is small yet touches the division of roles must not be neglected;
translations.idiomatic: Even small matters that bear on each office's proper role must not be neglected;

sentences.zh: 失之，則亂所由生。

translations.literal: once neglected, disorder is thereby born.
translations.idiomatic: neglect them and disorder follows.

sentences.zh: 遺、補雖卑，侍臣也，中丞雖高，法吏也；

translations.literal: Reminders and supplementation censors, though low in rank, are attending ministers; the vice censor-in-chief, though high, is a law officer;
translations.idiomatic: Reminders and supplementation censors are low in rank but still the emperor's attendants; the vice censor-in-chief is lofty but still a legal officer;

sentences.zh: 侍臣見陵則恭不廣，法吏自恣則法壞。

translations.literal: when attending ministers are bullied, reverence is not spread abroad; when law officers indulge themselves, the law is ruined.
translations.idiomatic: bully the attendants and respect withers; let legal officers run wild and the law collapses.

sentences.zh: 聞元和、長慶時，中丞呵止不半坊，今乃至兩坊，謂之籠街。

translations.literal: It is heard that in the Yuanhe and Changqing eras, when the vice censor-in-chief shouted to halt passage it was not half a ward; now it reaches two wards—called 'caging the street.
translations.idiomatic: Under Yuanhe and Changqing, a vice censor's runners cleared barely half a ward; now Zao clears two wards—people call it caging the street.

sentences.zh: 造擅自尊大，忽僭擬之嫌，請得論罪。」

translations.literal: Zao on his own authority is arrogant and grand, heedless of the suspicion of overstepping—we ask that he be judged guilty.
translations.idiomatic: Zao has grown arrogant beyond his station, inviting the suspicion of usurpation—we ask that he be punished.

sentences.zh: 帝乃詔臺官、供奉官共道路，聽先後行，相值則揖。

translations.literal: The emperor then ordered that censorate officials and palace attendants share the road, allowed to go first or after as they met, and when they encountered one another to bow.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then decreed that censors and palace attendants share the road, passing in order of arrival and bowing when they met.

sentences.zh: 中丞傳呼不得過三百步。

translations.literal: The vice censor-in-chief's runners calling the way might not go beyond three hundred paces.
translations.idiomatic: A vice censor's runners were limited to three hundred paces ahead.

sentences.zh: 造彈擊無所回畏，威望隱然，發南曹偽官九十人，主史皆論死。

translations.literal: Zao in impeachment knew no turning back or fear; his authority and prestige were quietly manifest. He exposed ninety false officials of the southern bureau; the chief clerks were all sentenced to death.
translations.idiomatic: In his impeachments Zao never flinched; his authority was felt throughout the capital. He exposed ninety bogus officials in the southern bureau and secured death sentences for the chief clerks.

sentences.zh: 遷尚書右丞，封祁縣子。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and enfeoffed as Viscount of Qixian.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to right vice director of the Department of State Affairs and enfeoffed as Viscount of Qixian.

sentences.zh: 興元軍亂，殺李絳，眾謂造可夷其亂，文宗亦以為能，乃授檢校右散騎常侍、山南西道節度使，許以便宜從事。

translations.literal: When the Xingyuan army mutinied and killed Li Jiang, the multitude said Zao could quell the disorder; Wenzong also considered him capable, and therefore appointed him Acting Right Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry and military commissioner of the Shannan West Circuit, allowing him to act as circumstances required.
translations.idiomatic: When mutiny broke out in the Xingyuan army and Li Jiang was killed, many said Zao could put down the revolt; Wenzong agreed and made him acting right attendant of scattered cavalry and military commissioner of Shannan West, with authority to act at discretion.

sentences.zh: 帝慮其勞費，造曰：「臣計諸道戍蠻之兵方還，願得密詔受約束，用此足矣。」

translations.literal: The emperor worried over the labor and expense; Zao said, "Your servant calculates that the troops garrisoning the barbarians on the various circuits are just returning—I wish to receive a secret edict binding them; using these will be sufficient.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor worried about cost; Zao said, "The frontier garrisons are just returning—I need only a secret edict to command them, and that will be enough.

sentences.zh: 許之。

translations.literal: This was granted.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 命神策將董仲質、河中將溫德彜、郃陽將劉士和從造。

translations.literal: He ordered the Shence general Dong Zhongzhi, the Hezhong general Wen Deyi, and the Heyang general Liu Shihe to follow Zao.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Shence general Dong Zhongzhi, Hezhong general Wen Deyi, and Heyang general Liu Shihe to accompany Zao.

sentences.zh: 而興元將衛誌忠、張丕、李少直自蜀還，造喻以意，皆曰：「不敢二。」

translations.literal: Meanwhile the Xingyuan generals Wei Zhizhong, Zhang Pi, and Li Shaozhi were returning from Shu; Zao explained his intent, and all said, "We dare not be of two minds.
translations.idiomatic: The Xingyuan generals Wei Zhizhong, Zhang Pi, and Li Shaozhi were returning from Shu; when Zao explained his plan they all pledged, "We will not waver.

sentences.zh: 乃用八百人自從，五百人為前軍。

translations.literal: He then took eight hundred men with him, five hundred as the vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: He took eight hundred men with him, five hundred as vanguard.

sentences.zh: 既入，前軍呵護諸門。

translations.literal: Once inside, the vanguard cleared and guarded every gate.
translations.idiomatic: On entering, the vanguard secured every gate.

sentences.zh: 造至，欲大宴，視聽事，曰：「此隘狹，不足饗士。」

translations.literal: When Zao arrived he wished to hold a great feast; he looked at the audience hall and said, "This is cramped and narrow—not enough to feast the officers.
translations.idiomatic: Zao arrived intending a great feast, inspected the audience hall, and said, "This hall is too cramped to entertain the troops properly.

sentences.zh: 更徙牙門。

translations.literal: They moved instead to the headquarters gate.
translations.idiomatic: They moved the gathering to the headquarters compound.

sentences.zh: 坐定，將卒羅拜，徐曰：「吾欲聞新軍去主意，可悉前，舊軍無得進。」

translations.literal: Once seated, officers and soldiers bowed in ranks; he said slowly, "I wish to hear the new army's reasons for leaving—let all of them come forward; the old army must not advance.
translations.idiomatic: When all were seated the troops bowed in ranks. Zao said deliberately, "I want to hear why the new troops mutinied—let them all come forward; the old troops must stay back.

sentences.zh: 勞問畢，就坐，酒行，從兵合，卒有覺者，欲引去，造傳言叱之，乃不敢動。

translations.literal: When the inquiries of courtesy were done they took their seats; as wine was passed the escort troops closed in; some soldiers sensed it and tried to slip away—Zao shouted orders and they did not dare move.
translations.idiomatic: After the formal greetings they sat down and wine was served; Zao's escort closed in. Some mutineers sensed the trap and tried to leave, but Zao's runners shouted them down and they froze.

sentences.zh: 即問軍中殺絳狀，誌忠、丕夾階立，拔劍傳呼曰：「悉殺之！」

translations.literal: He immediately asked about the killing of Jiang in the army; Zhizhong and Pi stood flanking the steps, drew swords, and called out, "Kill them all!
translations.idiomatic: He then demanded an account of Jiang's murder. Zhizhong and Pi stood on either side of the steps, drew their swords, and cried, "Kill them all!

sentences.zh: 圍兵爭奮，皆斬首，凡八百余人。

translations.literal: The surrounding troops strove in rivalry; all were beheaded—more than eight hundred in all.
translations.idiomatic: The surrounding troops fell upon them; more than eight hundred were beheaded.

sentences.zh: 親殺絳者，醢之；

translations.literal: Those who had personally killed Jiang were made into minced meat;
translations.idiomatic: Those who had killed Jiang with their own hands were minced;

sentences.zh: 號令者，殊死。

translations.literal: those who had given the orders were sentenced to death without mercy.
translations.idiomatic: those who had given the orders were executed without mercy.

sentences.zh: 取百級祭絳，三十級祭死事官王景延等，余悉投之漢江。

translations.literal: A hundred heads were taken to sacrifice to Jiang, thirty heads to sacrifice to the officials who died in service such as Wang Jingyan, and the rest were all cast into the Han River.
translations.idiomatic: A hundred heads were offered to Jiang's spirit, thirty to officials who had died in the crisis such as Wang Jingyan, and the rest were thrown into the Han River.

sentences.zh: 監軍楊叔元擁造靴祈哀，造以兵衛出之。

translations.literal: The army supervisor Yang Shuyuan clutched Zao's boots and begged for mercy; Zao had armed guards escort him out.
translations.idiomatic: Army supervisor Yang Shuyuan clutched Zao's boots and pleaded for his life; Zao had guards escort him away.

sentences.zh: 詔流康州。

translations.literal: An edict banished him to Kangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: An edict exiled him to Kangzhou.

sentences.zh: 叔元，始激兵亂者也，人以造不戮為恨。

translations.literal: Shuyuan was the one who had first incited the army mutiny; people resented that Zao did not execute him.
translations.idiomatic: Shuyuan had been the one who incited the mutiny, and many resented that Zao spared his life.

sentences.zh: 以功加檢校禮部尚書，賜萬縑賞其兵。

translations.literal: For his merit he was additionally made Acting Minister of Rites and granted ten thousand bolts of silk to reward his troops.
translations.idiomatic: For this service he was made acting minister of rites and given ten thousand bolts of silk to reward his men.

sentences.zh: 入為兵部侍郎，以病自言，出東都留守。

translations.literal: He entered court as Vice Minister of War; citing illness on his own initiative, he went out as defender of the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: He returned to court as vice minister of war, then citing illness became defender of the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 俄節度河陽。

translations.literal: Soon he became military commissioner of Heyang.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was made military commissioner of Heyang.

sentences.zh: 奏復懷州古秦渠枋口堰，以溉濟源、河內、溫、武陟四縣田五千頃。

translations.literal: He memorialized to restore the ancient Qin canal and Fangkou weir of Huaizhou, irrigating five thousand qing of fields in the four counties of Jiyuan, Henei, Wen, and Wuzhi.
translations.idiomatic: He petitioned to restore Huaizhou's ancient Qin canal and Fangkou weir, irrigating five thousand qing of farmland in Jiyuan, Henei, Wen, and Wuzhi.

sentences.zh: 召為御史大夫。

translations.literal: He was recalled as Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled as censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 方倚以相，會疾，不能朝，改禮部尚書。

translations.literal: He was just being relied on for the chancellorship when illness struck and he could not attend court; he was changed to Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was about to make him chief minister when illness kept him from court; he was transferred to minister of rites instead.

sentences.zh: 卒，年七十，贈尚書右僕射。

translations.literal: He died at seventy; posthumously he was made Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He died at seventy and was posthumously made right vice director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 兄邈，弟遜。

translations.literal: His elder brother was Miao; his younger brother was Xun.
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother was Miao and his younger brother Xun.

sentences.zh: 邈，長慶、大和中，累以拾遺、補闕召，不應。

translations.literal: Miao, in the Changqing and Dahe eras, was repeatedly summoned as Reminder and Supplementation Censor but did not respond.
translations.idiomatic: Miao was repeatedly summoned as reminder and supplementation censor during Changqing and Dahe but never accepted.

sentences.zh: 遜嘗為邑宰，解印綬去。

translations.literal: Xun once served as district magistrate, then removed his seal and sash and departed.
translations.idiomatic: Xun had once been a district magistrate but surrendered his seal and left office.

sentences.zh: 彥博裔孫廷筠，少敏悟，工為辭章，與李商隱皆有名，號「溫李」。

translations.literal: Yanbo's descendant Tingyun, quick and perceptive in youth, was skilled at literary composition; he and Li Shangyin were both famous, styled "Wen and Li."
translations.idiomatic: Yanbo's descendant Wen Tingyun was clever as a youth and skilled at verse; he and Li Shangyin were famed together as "Wen and Li."

sentences.zh: 然薄於行，無檢幅。

translations.literal: Yet he was shallow in conduct and without restraint.
translations.idiomatic: But his conduct was loose and unrestrained.

sentences.zh: 又多作側辭艷曲，與貴胄裴諴、令狐滈等蒲飲狎昵。

translations.literal: He also wrote many licentious lyrics and sensual songs, and with noble scions such as Pei Xian and Linghu Hao he drank on rush mats in intimate familiarity.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote many sensual songs and caroused intimately with young nobles such as Pei Xian and Linghu Hao.

sentences.zh: 數舉進士不中第。

translations.literal: He repeatedly presented himself for the jinshi examination but never passed.
translations.idiomatic: He took the jinshi examination many times without success.

sentences.zh: 思神速，多為人作文。

translations.literal: His thoughts were swift as a spirit; he often wrote compositions for others.
translations.idiomatic: His mind was extraordinarily quick, and he often ghost-wrote for others.

sentences.zh: 大中末，試有司，廉視尤謹，廷筠不樂，上書千余言，然私占授者已八人，執政鄙其為，授方山尉。

translations.literal: At the end of Dazhong, when the examination bureau tested candidates with especially strict integrity screening, Tingyun was displeased and submitted a memorial of more than a thousand words; yet those privately promised appointments already numbered eight, and the chief ministers despised his conduct and appointed him marshal of Fangshan.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of Dazhong the examination bureau screened candidates with unusual strictness; Tingyun was offended and submitted a thousand-word memorial, but eight candidates had already been privately promised posts, and the chief ministers, disgusted with him, made him marshal of Fangshan.

sentences.zh: 徐商鎮襄陽，署巡官，不得志，去歸江東。

translations.literal: When Xu Shang governed Xiangyang he appointed him touring officer; frustrated in his ambitions, he left and returned to the Jiangdong region.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Shang, governing Xiangyang, made him a touring officer, but frustrated, he left for the lower Yangtze.

sentences.zh: 令狐綯方鎮淮南，廷筠怨居中時不為助力，過府不肯謁。

translations.literal: Linghu Tao was then governing Huainan; Tingyun resented that when Tao was at court he had not helped him, and passing his headquarters refused to pay a visit.
translations.idiomatic: Linghu Tao was then governing Huainan; Tingyun resented that Tao had not helped him when at court, and when passing his headquarters refused to call on him.

sentences.zh: 丐錢揚子院，夜醉，為邏卒擊折其齒，訴於綯。

translations.literal: Begging money at the Yangzi compound, he was drunk at night and patrol soldiers broke his teeth; he complained to Tao.
translations.idiomatic: While begging money at the Yangzi depot he got drunk one night and patrol guards broke his teeth; he appealed to Tao.

sentences.zh: 綯為劾吏，吏具道其汙行，綯兩置之。

translations.literal: Tao had the officers impeached; the officers fully reported his filthy conduct, and Tao set the matter aside both times.
translations.idiomatic: Tao had the guards prosecuted; they detailed Tingyun's misconduct, but Tao let the matter drop both times.

sentences.zh: 事聞京師，廷筠遍見公卿，言為吏誣染。

translations.literal: When the affair reached the capital, Tingyun visited all the chief ministers and nobles, saying he had been slandered and smeared by the officers.
translations.idiomatic: When word reached the capital, Tingyun visited every senior official claiming the guards had framed him.

sentences.zh: 俄而徐商執政，頗右之，欲白用。

translations.literal: Soon Xu Shang took power and favored him considerably, wishing to report and employ him.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Xu Shang came to power, favored him, and meant to recommend him for office.

sentences.zh: 會商罷，楊收疾之，遂廢卒。

translations.literal: When Shang was dismissed, Yang Shou detested him, and he died in obscurity.
translations.idiomatic: But Shang fell from power, Yang Shou loathed him, and he died in obscurity.

sentences.zh: 本名岐，字飛卿。

translations.literal: His original name was Qi; his courtesy name was Feiqing.
translations.idiomatic: His original name was Qi; his courtesy name was Feiqing.

sentences.zh: 弟廷皓，咸通中，署徐州觀察使崔彥曾幕府。

translations.literal: His younger brother Tinghao, in the Xiantong era, was appointed to the staff of Cui Yanzeng, observation commissioner of Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Tinghao, during Xiantong, joined the staff of Cui Yanzeng, observation commissioner of Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 龐勛反，以刃脅廷皓，使為表求節度使，廷皓紿曰：「表聞天子，當為公信宿思之。」

translations.literal: When Pang Xun rebelled, he threatened Tinghao with a blade and made him draft a memorial requesting a military commission; Tinghao deceived him, saying, "Once the memorial reaches the Son of Heaven, I shall think it over carefully on your behalf for one or two nights.
translations.idiomatic: When Pang Xun rebelled he forced Tinghao at swordpoint to draft a petition for a military commission; Tinghao stalled him, saying, "Once the petition reaches the emperor I will think it over for a night or two on your behalf.

sentences.zh: 勛喜。

translations.literal: Xun was pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Xun was pleased.

sentences.zh: 歸與妻子決，明日復見，勛索表，倨答曰：「我豈以筆硯事汝邪？

translations.literal: He returned and took leave of his wife and children; the next day when he saw Xun again, Xun demanded the memorial; he answered haughtily, "Would I serve you with brush and inkstone?
translations.idiomatic: He went home to bid his family farewell; the next day, when Xun demanded the petition, he answered coldly, "Do you think I would serve you with pen and ink?

sentences.zh: 其速殺我。」

translations.literal: Kill me quickly.
translations.idiomatic: Kill me at once.

sentences.zh: 勛熟視笑曰：「儒生有膽邪，吾動眾百萬，無一人操檄乎！」

translations.literal: Xun stared at him a long while and laughed, saying, "A scholar has courage, eh? I have moved a host of a million—has not one man taken up the dispatch brush?"
translations.idiomatic: Xun stared at him and laughed, "A scholar with guts! I command a million men—has no one among them taken up a brush?"

sentences.zh: 囚之，更使周重草表。

translations.literal: He imprisoned him and had Zhou Chong draft the memorial instead.
translations.idiomatic: He imprisoned Tinghao and had Zhou Chong write the petition instead.

sentences.zh: 彥曾遇害，廷皓亦死，詔贈兵部郎中。

translations.literal: When Yanzeng was murdered, Tinghao also died; an edict posthumously made him Director in the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: When Yanzeng was killed, Tinghao died as well; the court posthumously made him a director in the Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 皇甫無逸，字仁儉，京兆萬年人。

translations.literal: Huangfu Wuyi, courtesy name Renjian, was a man of Wannian in Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Huangfu Wuyi, courtesy name Renjian, came from Wannian in the capital district.

sentences.zh: 父誕，隋并州總管府司馬，漢王諒反，逼之不從，見殺。

translations.literal: His father Dan served as marshal of the Bingzhou governorate headquarters under the Sui; when Prince Han Liang rebelled he was forced to join but refused and was killed.
translations.idiomatic: His father Dan was marshal of the Bingzhou governorate under the Sui; when Prince Han Liang rebelled he was pressed to join but refused and was executed.

sentences.zh: 無逸在長安，聞變即號慟，人問故，對曰：「吾父生平重節義，必無茍免者。

translations.literal: Wuyi was in Chang'an; on hearing of the upheaval he immediately wailed in grief. When people asked why, he replied, "My father all his life valued integrity and righteousness—he will certainly not seek a shameful escape.
translations.idiomatic: Wuyi was in Chang'an; when he heard the news he broke into mourning wails. Asked why, he said, "My father prized integrity all his life—he would never save himself at the cost of honor.

sentences.zh: 頃訃至，果然。

translations.literal: Before long the death notice arrived—it was indeed so.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the death notice arrived, and it was exactly as he had said.

sentences.zh: 時五等廢，煬帝嘉誕忠，特封無逸平輿侯，而贈誕柱國、弘義郡公。

translations.literal: At that time the five ranks were abolished; Emperor Yang praised Dan's loyalty and specially enfeoffed Wuyi as Marquis of Pingyu, while posthumously making Dan Pillar of State and Duke of Hongyi.
translations.idiomatic: The five noble ranks had been abolished, but Emperor Yang honored Dan's loyalty by specially enfeoffing Wuyi as Marquis of Pingyu and posthumously making Dan a pillar of state and Duke of Hongyi.

sentences.zh: 無逸歷淯陽太守，治為天下最，再遷右武衛將軍。

translations.literal: Wuyi served as prefect of Yuyang; his governance ranked first in the empire, and he was twice promoted to General of the Right Martial Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Wuyi served as prefect of Yuyang, where his administration was ranked the best in the empire; he was twice promoted to general of the right martial guard.

sentences.zh: 帝幸江都，詔居守洛陽。

translations.literal: When the emperor visited Jiangdu, an edict ordered him to remain and guard Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor went to Jiangdu, Wuyi was ordered to remain and guard Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 帝被殺，乃與段達、元文都立越王侗。

translations.literal: When the emperor was killed, he together with Duan Da and Yuan Wendu enthroned Prince Yue Tong.
translations.idiomatic: After the emperor was murdered, he joined Duan Da and Yuan Wendu in enthroning Prince Yue Tong.

sentences.zh: 及王世充篡，棄母妻，斬關自歸。

translations.literal: When Wang Shichong usurped power, he abandoned mother and wife, cut through the passes, and returned on his own to the Tang side.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Shichong seized power, he abandoned his mother and wife, broke through the passes, and fled back to Tang.

sentences.zh: 追騎及，無逸顧曰：「吾有死，終不能同爾為逆。」

translations.literal: Pursuing horsemen caught up; Wuyi looked back and said, "I have my death—I can never join you in rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Pursuers caught up; Wuyi turned and said, "I am ready to die—I will never join you in treason.

sentences.zh: 解金帶投之地，曰：「以與爾，無相困。」

translations.literal: He removed his gold belt and threw it to the ground, saying, "Take this for yourselves—do not press me."
translations.idiomatic: He unbuckled his gold belt and threw it down, saying, "Take this and leave me be."

sentences.zh: 騎爭下取，由是獲免。

translations.literal: The horsemen scrambled down to seize it, and thereby he escaped.
translations.idiomatic: The riders dismounted to grab the belt, and he escaped.

sentences.zh: 高祖以無逸本隋勛舊，尊遇之，拜刑部尚書，封滑國公。

translations.literal: Gaozu, because Wuyi was originally an old meritorious servant of the Sui, honored and treated him well, appointing him Minister of Justice and enfeoffing him as Duke of Huaguo.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu, knowing Wuyi as an old Sui loyalist, treated him with honor, made him minister of justice, and enfeoffed him as Duke of Huaguo.

sentences.zh: 歷陜東道行臺民部尚書，遷御史大夫。

translations.literal: He served as Minister of the Civil Branch on the Shandong East Circuit field headquarters, then was promoted to Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: He served as minister of the civil branch on the Shandong East headquarters, then became censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 時蜀新定，吏多橫恣，人不聊，詔無逸持節巡撫，得承制除吏。

translations.literal: At that time Shu had just been pacified; officials were mostly overbearing and lawless, and the people had no peace. An edict ordered Wuyi to tour and comfort the region bearing the imperial staff, with authority to appoint and dismiss officials by imperial commission.
translations.idiomatic: Shu had just been pacified, but officials were brutal and the people suffered; Wuyi was sent with imperial credentials to tour the region and given authority to appoint and dismiss officials.

sentences.zh: 既至，黜貪暴，用廉善，法令嚴明，蜀人以安。

translations.literal: Once he arrived he dismissed the greedy and violent and employed the honest and good; laws and orders were strict and clear, and the people of Shu were at peace.
translations.idiomatic: On arrival he removed the corrupt and violent, promoted the honest, enforced the law strictly, and brought peace to Shu.

sentences.zh: 皇甫希仁，憸人也，誣告無逸為母故陰交世充，帝判其詐，斬希仁，遣給事中李公昌馳諭。

translations.literal: Huangfu Xiren was a treacherous man who falsely accused Wuyi of secretly dealing with Shichong on account of his mother; the emperor judged it fraudulent, executed Xiren, and sent Attendant of the Secretariat Li Gongchang by urgent relay to reassure him.
translations.idiomatic: Huangfu Xiren, a schemer, falsely accused Wuyi of secret dealings with Shichong because of his mother; the emperor saw through the fraud, executed Xiren, and sent Li Gongchang posthaste to reassure Wuyi.

sentences.zh: 又有告無逸交通蕭銑者，時無逸與行臺僕射竇璡不協，因表自陳，並上璡罪。

translations.literal: There was also one who reported that Wuyi had dealings with Xiao Xian; at the time Wuyi was not on good terms with the field headquarters Vice Director Dou Jin, and therefore memorialized in his own defense while also reporting Jin's crimes.
translations.idiomatic: Another accused him of colluding with Xiao Xian; Wuyi was then at odds with headquarters vice director Dou Jin and memorialized in his own defense while also reporting Jin's offenses.

sentences.zh: 有詔劉世龍、溫彥博按之，無狀，遂斬告者而黜璡。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Liu Shilong and Wen Yanbo to investigate; there was no substance, and so the accuser was executed and Jin was demoted.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Shilong and Wen Yanbo were ordered to investigate; finding no evidence, the court executed the accuser and demoted Jin.

sentences.zh: 及還，帝勞曰：「比多譖毀，但以正直為佞人憎爾。」

translations.literal: On his return the emperor comforted him, saying, "Recently there has been much slander—but it is only because the upright are hated by flatterers.
translations.idiomatic: On his return the emperor consoled him, saying, "You have been slandered often—straightforward men are always hated by schemers.

sentences.zh: 無逸頓首謝，帝曰：「卿無負，何所謝？」

translations.literal: Wuyi bowed his head in thanks; the emperor said, "You have done no wrong—what is there to thank for?"
translations.idiomatic: Wuyi kowtowed in thanks; the emperor said, "You have done nothing wrong—why thank me?"

sentences.zh: 拜民部尚書，出為同州刺史，徙益州大都督府長史。

translations.literal: He was appointed Minister of the Civil Branch, went out as prefect of Tongzhou, and was transferred to chief administrator of the Yizhou Great Governorship headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: He was made minister of the civil branch, then prefect of Tongzhou, and later chief administrator of the Yizhou governorate.

sentences.zh: 所至輒閉閤不通賓客，左右無敢出入者；

translations.literal: Wherever he went he would close his doors and not receive guests; those around him did not dare to come and go;
translations.idiomatic: Wherever he served he shut his doors to visitors, and his attendants dared not come and go freely;

sentences.zh: 所須皆市易它境。

translations.literal: whatever he needed he purchased by trade in other jurisdictions.
translations.idiomatic: everything he needed he bought from other districts.

sentences.zh: 嘗按部，宿民家，鐙炷盡，主人將續進，無逸抽佩刀斷帶為炷，其廉介類如此。

translations.literal: Once on an inspection tour he lodged in a commoner's house; when the lamp wick was exhausted and the host was about to replenish it, Wuyi drew his belt knife, cut his belt for a wick, and acted with such integrity in like manner throughout.
translations.idiomatic: Once while on tour he stayed in a commoner's home; when the lamp went out and the host was about to relight it, Wuyi cut his belt with his dagger for a wick—his integrity ran to such lengths.

sentences.zh: 然過自畏慎，每上表疏，讀數十猶懼未審，使者上道，追省再三乃得遣。

translations.literal: Yet he was excessively self-cautious; each time he submitted a memorial he would read it dozens of times and still fear it was not thorough; when the messenger was on the road he would pursue and review it again and again before allowing dispatch.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he was excessively cautious: he would read each memorial dozens of times before sending it, and even after the courier had left would recall and review it again and again.

sentences.zh: 母在長安疾篤，太宗命馳驛召還承問，憂悸不能食，道病卒。

translations.literal: His mother in Chang'an fell gravely ill; Taizong ordered him summoned back by urgent relay to attend her; in grief and dread he could not eat, and on the road he died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother fell gravely ill in Chang'an, Taizong ordered him home by express courier; stricken with grief he could not eat and died on the road.

sentences.zh: 贈禮部尚書，謚曰孝。

translations.literal: Posthumously he was made Minister of Rites; his posthumous title was Xiao.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made minister of rites with the posthumous name Xiao (Filial).

sentences.zh: 王珪駁曰：「無逸入蜀，不能與母俱，留卒京師，子道未足稱，不可謂孝。」

translations.literal: Wang Gui objected, saying, "When Wuyi entered Shu he could not take his mother with him and left her to die in the capital—the way of a son is not sufficient to be praised; he cannot be called filial.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Gui objected, "Wuyi went to Shu without his mother and left her to die in the capital—his conduct as a son does not merit praise; he cannot be called filial.

sentences.zh: 乃更謚良。

translations.literal: His posthumous title was therefore changed to Liang.
translations.idiomatic: His posthumous name was changed to Liang (Good).

sentences.zh: 李襲誌，字重光。

translations.literal: Li Xizhi, courtesy name Chongguang.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xizhi, whose courtesy name was Chongguang.

sentences.zh: 其先本隴西狄道人，五世祖避地，更為金州安康人。

translations.literal: His ancestors were originally from Didao in Longxi; his fifth-generation ancestor fled the troubles and became a man of Ankang in Jinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His family originally came from Didao in Longxi; five generations back an ancestor fled turmoil and settled in Ankang, Jinzhou.

sentences.zh: 仕隋始安郡丞。

translations.literal: He served the Sui as assistant prefect of Shian Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Sui he served as assistant prefect of Shian.

sentences.zh: 大業末，盜賊起，襲誌傾私產募士，得三千人，乘城拒盜，蕭銑、林士弘屢攻之不下。

translations.literal: At the end of Daye bandits rose; Xizhi poured out his private wealth to recruit soldiers, obtaining three thousand men, manned the walls to resist the bandits, and though Xiao Xian and Lin Shihong repeatedly attacked they could not take it.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of Daye, when bandits rose, Xizhi spent his private fortune to raise three thousand men, held the walls against them, and repelled repeated attacks by Xiao Xian and Lin Shihong.

sentences.zh: 聞煬帝喪，乃與士民縞素三日臨，或說曰：「公臨郡久，士大夫悅向，蠻夷畏威，雖曰隋臣，實君長也。

translations.literal: On hearing of Emperor Yang's death, he and the gentry and people wore white mourning and observed three days of lamentation. Someone urged him, saying, "You have long governed the commandery; scholars and officials are pleased to turn to you, and the barbarians fear your authority—though called a Sui subject, you are in truth a lord and chief.
translations.idiomatic: When news came of Emperor Yang's death, he and the local elite mourned in white for three days. Someone urged him, "You have ruled here long; the gentry follow you and the tribes fear you—you are a true lord in all but name.

sentences.zh: 今四海分裂，自王者非一姓，宜遂據嶺表，取百粵，豈遽不若尉佗乎？」

translations.literal: Now the four seas are split; those who make themselves kings are not of one surname—you ought to seize the Lingnan region and take the Hundred Yue—would you suddenly be inferior to Zhao Tuo?
translations.idiomatic: The realm is divided; many claim kingship. You should hold Lingnan and take the Hundred Yue—why should you rank below Zhao Tuo?

sentences.zh: 襲誌曰：「吾世隋臣，今江都雖淪，宗社尚有奉，諸君當相與戮力刷仇恥，豈怙亂圖不義哉？

translations.literal: Xizhi said, "My family for generations has been subjects of the Sui; though Jiangdu has now fallen, the altars of state still have one who receives sacrifice—you gentlemen should together exert your strength to wash away enmity and shame—how could you cling to disorder and plot unrighteousness?
translations.idiomatic: Xizhi replied, "My family has served the Sui for generations. Though Jiangdu has fallen, the dynasty still has a claimant—you should join me in avenging this shame, not profit from chaos.

sentences.zh: 吾寧蹈忠死，不逆節以生，尉佗不足為吾法也。」

translations.literal: I would rather tread loyalty unto death than live by violating my integrity—Zhao Tuo is not fit to be my model."
translations.idiomatic: I would rather die loyal than live in rebellion—Zhao Tuo is no model for me."

sentences.zh: 欲斬說者，眾諫，乃止。

translations.literal: He wished to behead the persuader; the multitude remonstrated and he desisted.
translations.idiomatic: He meant to execute the adviser, but the crowd dissuaded him and he desisted.

sentences.zh: 遂固守凡二年，力窮援絕，為銑所陷，偽署工部尚書、桂州總管。

translations.literal: He then held firm for two years in all; strength exhausted and aid cut off, he was taken by Xian, who falsely appointed him Minister of Works and military governor of Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He held out for two years until strength and supplies failed; Xiao Xian captured him and gave him the false titles of minister of works and military governor of Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 武德初，高祖賜書，命其子玄嗣召之。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Wude Gaozu sent a letter ordering his son Xuansi to summon him.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Wude, Gaozu wrote ordering his son Xuansi to summon him.

sentences.zh: 襲誌約嶺南酋永平郡守李光度潛圖歸國。

translations.literal: Xizhi joined with the Lingnan chieftain Li Guangdu, prefect of Yongping, to plot secretly a return to the Tang state.
translations.idiomatic: Xizhi conspired with Li Guangdu, prefect of Yongping and a Lingnan leader, to return to Tang allegiance.

sentences.zh: 帝復以書諭曰：「公朕之宗，不可與異姓比，宜及子弟並豫宗正屬籍。」

translations.literal: The emperor again wrote instructing him, saying, "You are of my clan—you cannot be compared with those of other surnames; you and your sons and younger brothers should all be entered in the registers of the Imperial Clan Court.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wrote again, "You are of my clan, not to be ranked with outsiders; you and your sons should be entered in the imperial clan registers.

sentences.zh: 乃銑平，嶺南六十余州皆送款，襲誌誘而致雲。

translations.literal: Then Xian was pacified; more than sixty prefectures of Lingnan all sent pledges of submission, which Xizhi enticed and brought in.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiao Xian fell, more than sixty Lingnan prefectures submitted, largely through Xizhi's persuasion.

sentences.zh: 趙郡王孝恭承制授桂州總管。

translations.literal: The Prince of Zhao Jun, Xiaogong, by imperial commission appointed him military governor of Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Xiaogong of Zhao commissioned him military governor of Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 五年來朝，進柱國，封始安郡公、江州都督。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he came to court, was advanced to Pillar of State, and enfeoffed as Duke of Shian while made military governor of Jiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he came to court, was made pillar of state, enfeoffed as Duke of Shian, and appointed military governor of Jiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 後討輔公祏，為水軍總管，轉桂州都督。

translations.literal: Later, in the campaign against Fu Gongshi, he served as commander of the naval forces, then was transferred to military governor of Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Later, campaigning against Fu Gongshi, he commanded the naval forces, then returned as military governor of Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 襲誌守桂二十八年，政尚清省，南荒便之。

translations.literal: Xizhi guarded Guizhou for twenty-eight years; his government prized clarity and economy, and the southern wilds were benefited.
translations.idiomatic: Xizhi governed Guizhou for twenty-eight years with a spare, honest administration that benefited the southern frontier.

sentences.zh: 表請入朝，以光祿大夫、汾州刺史致仕，卒。

translations.literal: He memorialized requesting to come to court, was made Grand Master for Splendid Happiness and retired as prefect of Fenzhou, then died.
translations.idiomatic: He petitioned to come to court, retired as grand master for splendid happiness and prefect of Fenzhou, and died.

sentences.zh: 弟襲譽，字茂實，通敏有識度。

translations.literal: His younger brother Xiyu, styled Maoshi, was penetratingly quick-witted and possessed discernment.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Xiyu, courtesy name Maoshi, was clever and far-sighted.

sentences.zh: 仕隋為冠軍府司兵。

translations.literal: He served the Sui as quartermaster of the Champion [Generals'] Mansion.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Sui he served as quartermaster of the Champion General's staff.

sentences.zh: 陰世師輔代王守京師也，三輔盜螘聚，襲譽請以兵據永豐倉，發粟賑窮乏，出庫物賞戰士，馳檄郡縣，共逐捕賊。

translations.literal: When Yin Shishi aided the Prince of Dai in holding the capital, bandits in the three metropolises swarmed like ants; Xiyu requested to take troops to seize Yongfeng Granary, distribute grain to relieve the destitute, issue storehouse goods to reward warriors, and dispatch urgent proclamations to commanderies and counties to join in pursuing and capturing the robbers together.
translations.idiomatic: While Yin Shishi was helping the Prince of Dai defend Chang'an, rebels swarmed through the capital region like ants. Xiyu proposed seizing Yongfeng Granary with troops, issuing grain to the destitute, distributing storehouse goods to reward the soldiers, and sending urgent dispatches to the commanderies and counties to join in hunting down the bandits.

sentences.zh: 世師不從。

translations.literal: Shishi did not follow [his advice].
translations.idiomatic: Shishi refused to act on it.

sentences.zh: 乃求出募山南兵，至漢中，高祖已定長安，召授太府少卿、安康郡公。

translations.literal: Thereupon he sought leave to go out and recruit troops from the southern mountains; reaching Hanzhong, the Founding Emperor had already secured Chang'an and summoned him, appointing him Vice Minister of the Imperial Storehouse and Duke of Ankang.
translations.idiomatic: He then obtained permission to raise troops in the southern mountains, but by the time he reached Hanzhong the emperor had already taken Chang'an. Xiyu was summoned and made Vice Minister of the Imperial Granary and Duke of Ankang.

sentences.zh: 伐王世充也，拜潞州總管。

translations.literal: When [the court] campaigned against Wang Shichong, he was appointed overall commander of Lu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: During the campaign against Wang Shichong, he was appointed military governor of Lu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 時突厥已和親，又通使世充，襲譽捕斬之。

translations.literal: At that time the Turks had already concluded a marriage alliance [with Tang], yet also sent envoys to Shichong; Xiyu captured and beheaded them.
translations.idiomatic: The Turks had already made peace with the Tang through marriage, yet they also sent envoys to Wang Shichong. Xiyu seized the envoys and beheaded them.

sentences.zh: 詔委典運，以饟東軍。

translations.literal: An edict entrusted him with managing transport to supply the eastern army.
translations.idiomatic: He was ordered to oversee logistics and provision the eastern armies.

sentences.zh: 擢累揚州大都督府長史、江南巡察大使，多所黜陟。

translations.literal: He was promoted in succession to Chief Administrator of the Yangzhou Grand Protectorate and Commissioner for Inspecting Jiangnan, and dismissed and appointed many [officials].
translations.idiomatic: He rose to become chief administrator of Yangzhou and commissioner for inspecting the Jiangnan circuit, promoting and dismissing numerous officials.

sentences.zh: 揚州，江、吳大都會，俗喜商賈，不事農；

translations.literal: Yangzhou was a great metropolis of the Jiang and Wu regions; custom favored merchants and neglected agriculture.
translations.idiomatic: Yangzhou was the great commercial hub of the lower Yangtze, where the people favored trade over farming.

sentences.zh: 襲譽為引雷陂水，築句城塘，溉田八百頃，以盡地利，民多歸本。

translations.literal: Xiyu led in water from Lei Marsh, built the Jucheng embankment, and irrigated eight hundred qing of fields, thereby fully exploiting the land's advantage; the people mostly returned to their basic occupation.
translations.idiomatic: He channeled water from Lei Marsh, built the Jucheng reservoir, and irrigated eight hundred qing of fields, bringing the land fully into use. Many people returned to farming.

sentences.zh: 召為太府卿。

translations.literal: He was summoned [to court] as Minister of the Imperial Storehouse.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to the capital as Minister of the Imperial Granary.

sentences.zh: 為人嚴愨，以威肅聞。

translations.literal: As a man he was stern and cautious, and was known for awe-inspiring severity.
translations.idiomatic: He was stern and disciplined, renowned for his formidable bearing.

sentences.zh: 居家儉，厚於宗親，祿稟隨多少散之。

translations.literal: At home he was frugal, yet generous toward kinsmen, dispersing his salary and grain allowance according to whatever amount he had.
translations.idiomatic: He lived frugally at home but was generous to his kin, sharing his salary and grain allowances with them as soon as he received them.

sentences.zh: 以余資寫書，罷揚州，書遂數事載。

translations.literal: With surplus funds he copied books; when he left Yangzhou, his books finally filled several transport carts.
translations.idiomatic: He used his spare income to copy books; by the time he left Yangzhou, his library filled several cartloads.

sentences.zh: 嘗謂子孫曰：「吾性不喜財，遂至窶乏。

translations.literal: He once told his sons and grandsons: "By nature I do not delight in wealth, and thus have come to destitution.
translations.idiomatic: He once told his descendants, "I have never cared for money, and so I have ended up poor.

sentences.zh: 然負京有賜田十頃，能耕之，足以食；

translations.literal: Yet near the capital I have ten qing of granted fields; if you can till them, they will suffice for food.
translations.idiomatic: Yet near the capital I own ten qing of granted land. If you farm it diligently, you will have enough to eat.

sentences.zh: 河內千樹桑，事之可以衣；

translations.literal: In Henei are a thousand mulberry trees; tending them can clothe you.
translations.idiomatic: In Henei there are a thousand mulberry trees; work them and you will have clothes.

sentences.zh: 江都書，力讀可進求宦。

translations.literal: The books at Jiangdu—if you read them with effort you may advance and seek office.
translations.idiomatic: The books I left at Jiangdu—study them hard and you can make your way in official life.

sentences.zh: 吾歿後，能勤此，無資於人矣。」

translations.literal: After my death, if you can be diligent in these matters, you will need no support from others.
translations.idiomatic: After I am gone, if you work at these three things, you will never need to depend on anyone.

sentences.zh: 遷涼州都督，改同州刺史。

translations.literal: ["]He was transferred to be Protector-General of Liangzhou, then changed to Governor of Tong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was made protector-general of Liangzhou and later governor of Tong Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 坐在涼州以私憾杖殺番禾丞劉武，當死，廢為民，流泉州，卒。

translations.literal: He was convicted for in Liangzhou beating to death Fanhe Assistant Magistrate Liu Wu by staff over a personal grudge; he should have died, but was demoted to commoner status, exiled to Quanzhou, and died there.
translations.idiomatic: He was found guilty of beating to death Fanhe Assistant Magistrate Liu Wu over a private grievance while serving in Liangzhou. Sentenced to death, he was instead stripped of rank, exiled to Quanzhou, and died there.

sentences.zh: 姜謨，秦州上邽人。

translations.literal: Jiang Mo was a native of Shanggui in Qin Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Mo was a native of Shanggui in Qinzhou.

sentences.zh: 隋大業末，為晉陽長。

translations.literal: At the end of the Sui Daye reign era, he served as magistrate of Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Sui, he served as magistrate of Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 高祖在太原，謨前識之，謂所親曰：「隋政亂將亡，必有聖人受之。

translations.literal: When the Founding Emperor was at Taiyuan, Mo had known him earlier; he told those close to him: "Sui government is chaotic and about to perish; there must be a sage who will receive the Mandate.
translations.idiomatic: When the future emperor was stationed at Taiyuan, Mo, who had known him before, told his intimates, "The Sui regime is collapsing. A sage will surely receive the Mandate.

sentences.zh: 唐公負王霸資度，其必撥亂得天下。」

translations.literal: The Duke of Tang bears the capacity for kingship and hegemony; he will surely restore order and gain the realm.
translations.idiomatic: The Duke of Tang has the makings of a true ruler. He will surely restore order and win the empire.

sentences.zh: 乃深自結。

translations.literal: ["]Thereupon he bound himself to him deeply.
translations.idiomatic: He then attached himself to the duke with all his heart.

sentences.zh: 及大將軍府建，引為司功參軍，從平霍邑、絳郡，兵遂度河，謨部勒一夕濟，高祖嘆其略。

translations.literal: When the Grand General's Office was established, he was brought in as Registrar of Works; he followed in pacifying Huoyi and Jiang Commandery, and when the army crossed the river, Mo organized the crossing and in one night completed the ford; the Founding Emperor marveled at his strategy.
translations.idiomatic: When the Grand General's headquarters was set up, he was made registrar of works. He followed the campaigns that pacified Huoyi and Jiang Commandery, and when the army had to cross the Yellow River, Mo organized the crossing and got the entire force over in a single night. The emperor praised his resourcefulness.

sentences.zh: 進平長安，除相國胄曹參軍、長道縣公。

translations.literal: Advancing to pacify Chang'an, he was appointed Aide in the Chancellor's Bureau of Military Staff and Duke of Changdao.
translations.idiomatic: After Chang'an was taken, he was made aide in the chancellor's bureau of military staff and enfeoffed as Duke of Changdao.

sentences.zh: 子確。

translations.literal: His son Que.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Que.

sentences.zh: 確，字行本，以字顯。

translations.literal: Que, styled Xingben, was known by his style name.
translations.idiomatic: Que, courtesy name Xingben, was known by that name.

sentences.zh: 貞觀中，為將作少匠，護作九成、洛陽宮及諸苑禦，以幹力稱，多所賚嘗，遊幸無不從，遷宣威將軍。

translations.literal: In the Zhenguan era he served as Vice Director of Palace Construction, overseeing the building of the Jiucheng [Palace], Luoyang Palace, and the various imperial park residences; he was famed for practical ability, received many rewards, and on every imperial tour he was never absent; he was transferred to General Who Displays Might.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhenguan reign he served as vice director of palace construction, supervising work on the Jiucheng Palace, Luoyang Palace, and the imperial park residences. Renowned for his practical skill, he received many rewards and never missed an imperial tour. He was promoted to general who displays might.

sentences.zh: 太宗選趫才，衣五色袍，乘六閑馬，直屯營，宿衛仗內，號曰「飛騎」，每出幸，即以從，拜行本左屯衛將軍，分典之。

translations.literal: Taizong selected men of exceptional talent, clothed them in five-colored robes, mounted them on six fine horses, stationed them directly in the encampments, and had them guard within the weaponry; they were called "Flying Cavalry," and on every outing he took them along; Xingben was appointed General of the Left Garrison Guard and put in charge of them.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong selected exceptional men, dressed them in robes of five colors, mounted them on fine horses, and billeted them in the camps as an inner guard called the Flying Cavalry, who accompanied him on every outing. Xingben was made general of the left garrison guard and placed in command of them.

sentences.zh: 高昌之役，為行軍副總管，出伊州，距柳谷百里，依山造攻械，增損舊法，械益精。

translations.literal: In the Gaochang campaign he served as deputy commander of the campaign army, setting out from Yi Prefecture; a hundred li from Liugu, he built siege engines along the mountains, revising the old methods by additions and subtractions, and the engines grew ever more refined.
translations.idiomatic: During the campaign against Gaochang he served as deputy commander, advancing from Yi Prefecture. A hundred li from Liugu Valley he built siege engines along the mountain slopes, improving on the old designs until the machines were exceptionally refined.

sentences.zh: 其處有漢班超紀功碑，行本磨去古刻，更刊頌陳國威靈。
