translations.literal: At that place was the Han stele commemorating Ban Chao's achievements; Xingben ground away the ancient inscription and had carved in its place a hymn praising the state's majesty and spirit.
translations.idiomatic: There stood a Han stele commemorating Ban Chao's achievements. Xingben effaced the ancient inscription and had a new text carved praising the Tang state's power and glory.

sentences.zh: 遂與侯君集進平高昌，戰有功，璽書尉勞。

translations.literal: Thereupon with Hou Junji he advanced and pacified Gaochang; in battle he had merit, and an imperial letter of seal-script comforted and rewarded him.
translations.idiomatic: He then advanced with Hou Junji and pacified Gaochang, distinguishing himself in battle. The emperor sent a sealed letter of commendation.

sentences.zh: 還，為金城郡公，賜奴婢七十人，帛百五十段。

translations.literal: On his return he was made Duke of Jincheng Commandery, granted seventy male and female slaves, and a hundred fifty bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he was enfeoffed as Duke of Jincheng and given seventy slaves and a hundred fifty bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 帝將征高麗，行本諫未宜輕用師，不從。

translations.literal: When the emperor was about to campaign against Goguryeo, Xingben remonstrated that troops should not be lightly employed; [the emperor] did not follow [his advice].
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor prepared to campaign against Goguryeo, Xingben urged that the army not be committed lightly. The emperor did not heed him.

sentences.zh: 至蓋牟城，中流矢，卒。

translations.literal: Reaching Gaimou City, he was struck by a flying arrow and died.
translations.idiomatic: At Gaimou City he was struck by an arrow and died.

sentences.zh: 帝賦詩悼之，贈左衛大將軍、郕國公，謚曰襄，陪葬昭陵。

translations.literal: The emperor composed a poem to mourn him, posthumously appointing him Grand General of the Left Guard and Duke of the State of Xing, with posthumous title Xiang, and burial attendant at Zhaoling.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor composed a poem in his memory and posthumously made him grand general of the left guard and Duke of Xing, with the posthumous name Xiang, and had him buried near Zhaoling.

sentences.zh: 子簡嗣。

translations.literal: His son Jian succeeded [to the title].
translations.idiomatic: His son Jian succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 行本性恪敏。

translations.literal: Xingben by nature was respectful and keen.
translations.idiomatic: Xingben was by nature diligent and alert.

sentences.zh: 所居官，雖祈寒烈暑無懈容，加有巧思，凡朝之營繕，所司必諮而後行。

translations.literal: In whatever office he held, though in bitter cold or fierce heat he showed no slackness in demeanor; moreover he had ingenious ideas, and for all court construction and repair the responsible offices had to consult him before acting.
translations.idiomatic: In every post he held he never slackened, whether in bitter cold or fierce heat. He was also ingenious in design, and for all palace construction and repairs the responsible offices had to consult him before proceeding.

sentences.zh: 魏徵見其倚昵，恐浸啟侈端，勸帝斥之，帝賴其強濟，不斥也。

translations.literal: Wei Zheng saw his intimacy and favor [with the emperor], feared it would gradually open the way to extravagance, and urged the emperor to dismiss him; the emperor relied on his strong practical ability and did not dismiss him.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zheng saw how close he had grown to the emperor and feared this would encourage extravagance. He urged the emperor to dismiss Xingben, but the emperor valued his practical ability and kept him on.

sentences.zh: 子柔遠，美姿容，敷奏詳辯。

translations.literal: His son Rouyuan had handsome features and presented memorials in detail and with eloquence.
translations.idiomatic: His son Rouyuan was handsome and delivered memorials with polished eloquence.

sentences.zh: 武後時，至左鷹揚衛將軍，攝地官尚書通事舍人、內供奉。

translations.literal: In Empress Wu's time he rose to General of the Left Hawk-and-Banner Guard, acting as Master of Communications for the Minister of the Earth Bureau and Inner Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Under Empress Wu he rose to general of the left hawk-and-banner guard, serving concurrently as master of communications to the minister of the earth bureau and as inner attendant.

sentences.zh: 子皎、晦。

translations.literal: His sons Jiao and Hui.
translations.idiomatic: His sons were Jiao and Hui.

sentences.zh: 後將誅竇懷貞等，皎與密議，以功進殿中監、楚國公，食封四百戶。

translations.literal: Later, when [the emperor] was about to execute Dou Huaizhen and others, Jiao joined in secret deliberation; for his merit he was advanced to Director of the Palace Directorate and Duke of the State of Chu, with a fief of four hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor later moved to execute Dou Huaizhen and his faction, Jiao took part in the secret planning. For his service he was made director of the palace directorate and Duke of Chu, with a fief of four hundred households.

sentences.zh: 議者譏短皎任遇太過，帝以其籓邸舊，思有以宣布之，乃下詔曰：「殿中監、楚國公皎，往事朕於籓國，雖彭祖同書，子陵共學，不過也。

translations.literal: Critics faulted Jiao's appointment and favor as excessive; because he was an old companion from the princely residence, the emperor wished to make a public declaration and thereupon issued an edict saying: "Director of the Palace Directorate and Duke of the State of Chu Jiao—in former days serving Us in the princely state, though Pengzu studied the same books and Ziling studied together, it was no more than that.
translations.idiomatic: Critics complained that Jiao had been favored too lavishly. Because he was an old companion from the prince's household, the emperor wished to make his merits plain and issued an edict: "Director of the palace directorate and Duke of Chu Jiao served me in my princely days. Our bond was no greater than that of Pengzu studying the same texts or of Ziling as a fellow student.

sentences.zh: 朕嘗遊長楊、鄠、杜間，皎於時奉侍，數謂朕曰：『相王必登天位，王且儲副。』

translations.literal: We once toured between Changyang, E, and Du; Jiao at that time attended Us, repeatedly telling Us: 'The Prince of Xiang will surely ascend the imperial throne, and Your Highness will be heir apparent.'
translations.idiomatic: When I once traveled between Changyang, E, and Du, Jiao attended me and repeatedly said, 'The Prince of Xiang will surely take the throne, and you will be crown prince.'

sentences.zh: 朕叱而後止，復言於朕兄弟近戚。

translations.literal: [']We rebuked him and only then did he stop, yet he spoke again to Our brothers and close kin.
translations.idiomatic: I rebuked him and he stopped, but he went on saying the same to my brothers and close kin.

sentences.zh: 語聞太上皇，太上皇奏之中宗，遣嗣虢王邕等鞫問，皎一意保護，罔或貳言。

translations.literal: The words reached the Retired Emperor; the Retired Emperor reported them to Zhongzong, who sent the heir to the Prince of Guo Yong and others to interrogate; Jiao with single-minded intent protected [Us], without any second word.
translations.idiomatic: Word reached the retired emperor, who reported the matter to Zhongzong. Zhongzong sent the heir to the Prince of Guo, Yong, and others to interrogate Jiao, but Jiao steadfastly shielded me and never wavered in his testimony.

sentences.zh: 宗楚客、紀處訥等請投皎炎荒，中宗特詔貶潤州長史。

translations.literal: Zong Chuke, Ji Chuna, and others requested to cast Jiao into the fiery wastes; Zhongzong by special edict demoted him to Chief Administrator of Run Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Zong Chuke, Ji Chuna, and others urged that Jiao be banished to the southern wilds, but Zhongzong issued a special edict demoting him only to chief administrator of Run Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 專以忠力戴朕，謂天且有命，故履危蹈艱而無變焉。

translations.literal: He devoted himself with loyalty and strength to uphold Us, believing that Heaven moreover had a mandate, and therefore trod danger and hardship without change.
translations.idiomatic: He devoted himself wholly to supporting me, believing Heaven had ordained my rise, and so faced danger and hardship without faltering.

sentences.zh: 朕既即位，又參誅奸臣，將厚以光寵，每所捴遜。

translations.literal: Since We ascended the throne, he again took part in executing treacherous ministers; We intended to heap glory and favor upon him, yet on every occasion he declined.
translations.idiomatic: After I took the throne he again helped destroy treacherous ministers. I meant to reward him lavishly, but he declined every honor I offered.

sentences.zh: 造膝匪躬，舉多規益。

translations.literal: Coming to Our knee without regard for self, his proposals were mostly admonitions of benefit.
translations.idiomatic: He came to my side without thought for himself, and most of what he offered were useful remonstrances.

sentences.zh: 而悠悠之談，醜正惡直，天下之人，其未及識皎之功，何見之異也？

translations.literal: Yet idle talk slanders the upright and hates the straight; the people under Heaven have not yet come to know Jiao's achievements—why should their views differ [from Ours]?
translations.idiomatic: Yet idle gossip slanders the upright and hates the honest. The people of the realm have not yet grasped Jiao's merits—why should their judgment differ from mine?

sentences.zh: 昔漢昭之任霍光，魏祖之明程昱，朕之不德，庶幾於此。

translations.literal: Formerly Han Zhao entrusted Huo Guang; Wei Zu was clear-sighted regarding Cheng Yu—Our lack of virtue may perhaps approach this.
translations.idiomatic: Han Zhao entrusted Huo Guang; Cao Cao recognized Cheng Yu's worth. In my lesser way, I hope I may do the same.

sentences.zh: 且否當其悔，則必滅乃宗；

translations.literal: Moreover, when obstruction meets its time for regret, then one's clan must perish.
translations.idiomatic: When obstruction meets its hour of regret, an entire clan is destroyed.

sentences.zh: 泰至於亨，則所酬未補。

translations.literal: When great peace reaches to prosperity, then what is repaid does not make up [for the service].
translations.idiomatic: When great peace gives way to flourishing, the reward can never fully repay the debt.

sentences.zh: 豈流言之聽，而厚德之忘哉？

translations.literal: How could one heed floating words and forget deep virtue?
translations.idiomatic: Shall I heed idle rumor and forget deep obligation?

sentences.zh: 茍謀始有之，圖終可也。」

translations.literal: If one plans the beginning well, the end may be achieved.
translations.idiomatic: If the beginning is planned well, the end may be secured.

sentences.zh: 尋遷太常卿，監修國史。

translations.literal: ["]Shortly thereafter he was transferred to Minister of Ceremonies and supervised the compilation of the national history.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was made minister of ceremonies and put in charge of compiling the national history.

sentences.zh: 弟晦又為吏部侍郎，有權寵，宋璟以為非久安策，請抑損之。

translations.literal: His younger brother Hui was again Vice Minister of the Ministry of Personnel and held power and favor; Song Jing considered this not a policy for long peace and requested to reduce and restrain them.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Hui also served as vice minister of personnel and wielded great influence. Song Jing regarded this as unsound for the long term and urged that their power be curbed.

sentences.zh: 開元五年，下詔放歸田裏，使自娛。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Kaiyuan, an edict released them to return to their rural estates to amuse themselves.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Kaiyuan an edict sent them back to their home estates to live at leisure.

sentences.zh: 久之，復為秘書監。

translations.literal: After a long while, [Jiao] was again made Director of the Palace Library.
translations.idiomatic: After some time Jiao was again made director of the palace library.

sentences.zh: 十年，坐泄禁中語，為嗣濮王嶠所劾，敕中書門下究狀。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, he was convicted for leaking words from within the forbidden precincts; he was impeached by the heir to the Prince of Pu Qiao, and an edict ordered the Secretariat and Chancellery to investigate the facts.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he was charged with leaking palace secrets after being impeached by the heir to the Prince of Pu, Qiao. The emperor ordered the secretariat and chancellery to investigate.

sentences.zh: 嶠亦王守一姻家，中書令張嘉貞陰希其意，傅致皎獄。

translations.literal: Qiao was also a relation by marriage of Wang Shouyi; Chief Minister Zhang Jiazhen secretly hoped to please his intent and fabricated charges to bring Jiao into prison.
translations.idiomatic: Qiao was also related by marriage to Wang Shouyi. Chief minister Zhang Jiazhen secretly wished to please him and manufactured charges to imprison Jiao.

sentences.zh: 詔免殊死，杖之，流欽州。

translations.literal: An edict spared him from execution by special grace, had him beaten with the staff, and exiled him to Qin Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: An edict spared him from death, had him beaten, and exiled him to Qin Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 道病死，年五十。

translations.literal: On the road he died of illness, aged fifty.
translations.idiomatic: He died of illness on the road to exile, aged fifty.

sentences.zh: 親厚坐謫死者數人，世以為冤。

translations.literal: Several of his close intimates died through conviction and banishment; the age considered it an injustice.
translations.idiomatic: Several of his close associates died as a result of the purge, and the world regarded it as a grave injustice.

sentences.zh: 時源乾曜方侍中，不能正，為人所譏詆。

translations.literal: At that time Yuan Qianyao was serving as Palace Attendant but could not set things right, and was reviled by others.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Qianyao was then serving as palace attendant but could not set matters right, and was widely criticized.

sentences.zh: 帝後思皎舊勛，令遞柩還，以禮葬之，存問其家，追贈澤州刺史。

translations.literal: Later the emperor recalled Jiao's old merit, ordered the bier conveyed back, buried him with rites, sent inquiries to his family, and posthumously appointed him Governor of Ze Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor later remembered Jiao's old service, had his coffin brought back, buried him with full honors, sent condolences to his family, and posthumously made him governor of Ze Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 後以子尚主，更贈吏部尚書，仍賜封二百戶為祠享費。

translations.literal: Later, because his son married an imperial princess, he was further posthumously made Minister of the Ministry of Personnel, and a fief of two hundred households was still granted as funds for sacrificial offerings.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when his son married an imperial princess, Jiao was further posthumously made minister of personnel, and a fief of two hundred households was granted to support his family's ancestral rites.

sentences.zh: 故事，太常職奉陵廟。

translations.literal: By precedent, the Minister of Ceremonies' duty was to attend the imperial tombs and ancestral temples.
translations.idiomatic: By precedent the minister of ceremonies was responsible for tending the imperial tombs and ancestral temples.

sentences.zh: 開元末，濮陽王徹為宗正卿，有寵，始請宗正奉陵。

translations.literal: At the end of Kaiyuan, the Prince of Puyang Che served as Director of the Imperial Clan and was favored; he first requested that the Imperial Clan Directorate attend the tombs.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Kaiyuan era the Prince of Puyang, Che, served as director of the imperial clan and was in favor. He first petitioned that the clan directorate take charge of the tombs.

sentences.zh: 天寶中，張垍以主婿任太常，故復舊。

translations.literal: In the Tianbao era, Zhang Yan, as son-in-law of a princess, held the post of Minister of Ceremonies, and therefore the old arrangement was restored.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tianbao era Zhang Yan, as an imperial son-in-law, served as minister of ceremonies, and the old arrangement was restored.

sentences.zh: 及慶初敗，又以陵廟歸宗正雲。

translations.literal: When Qingchu fell, the tombs and temples were again returned to the Imperial Clan Directorate.
translations.idiomatic: When Qingchu fell from power, responsibility for the tombs and temples was again returned to the imperial clan directorate.

sentences.zh: 晦，起家蒲州參軍，累為高陵令，治有聲，遷長安令，人畏愛之。

translations.literal: Hui began his career as an aide in Pu Prefecture, was promoted in succession to Magistrate of Gaoling—his governance had a reputation—and was transferred to Magistrate of Chang'an; the people both feared and loved him.
translations.idiomatic: Hui began as an aide in Pu Prefecture and rose to magistrate of Gaoling, where his administration won renown. He was then made magistrate of Chang'an, and the people both feared and loved him.

sentences.zh: 開元初，擢御史中丞。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaiyuan he was promoted to Vice Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Kaiyuan era he was promoted to vice censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 先是，永徽、顯慶時，御史不拜宰相，銜命使四方者，廷中揖見，後稍屈下。

translations.literal: Previously, in the Yonghui and Xianqing eras, censors did not bow to chancellors; those bearing imperial orders to the four directions met them with a bow in the court hall—later [the censors] gradually bowed lower.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, during the Yonghui and Xianqing reigns, censors did not bow to chancellors, and envoys commissioned to the provinces met them with a bow in court. Later this ceremony was gradually diminished.

sentences.zh: 至晦，獨徇舊體，謂御史曰：「不如故事，且奏譴公等。」

translations.literal: When it came to Hui, he alone followed the old forms, telling the censors: "If you do not follow precedent, I shall memorialize to reprimand you gentlemen.
translations.idiomatic: Hui alone upheld the old protocol. He told the censors, "If you do not follow precedent, I shall memorialize the throne to reprimand you.

sentences.zh: 由是臺儀復振。

translations.literal: ["]Thereby the censorate's ceremonial dignity was restored.
translations.idiomatic: The censorate's dignity was thereby restored.

sentences.zh: 轉太常少卿。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Vice Minister of Ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to vice minister of ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 時國馬乏，晦請以詔書市馬六胡州，率得馬三千，署遊擊將軍，詔可。

translations.literal: At that time the state's horses were depleted; Hui requested to use an edict to purchase horses in the Six Hu Prefectures, and in the end obtained three thousand horses; he was appointed General of Mobile Striking Forces, and the edict approved.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the imperial stables were depleted. Hui petitioned to purchase horses in the Six Hu prefectures by imperial edict and ultimately obtained three thousand head. He was appointed general of mobile striking forces, and the edict was approved.

sentences.zh: 閑廄乃稍備。

translations.literal: The spare stables were thereby gradually replenished.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial stables were gradually brought back to strength.

sentences.zh: 除黃門侍郎，辭不拜，改兵部。

translations.literal: He was appointed Vice Minister of the Yellow Gate but declined to accept the appointment; he was changed to the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed vice minister of the yellow gate but declined the post and was transferred to the ministry of war.

sentences.zh: 滿歲，為吏部侍郎，主選。

translations.literal: When his term was complete, he became Vice Minister of the Ministry of Personnel and presided over selections.
translations.idiomatic: When his term expired he was made vice minister of personnel and placed in charge of official appointments.

sentences.zh: 曹史嘗請托為奸，前領選者周棘扈籓，檢窒內外，猶不禁。

translations.literal: The clerks of the bureau often sought patronage to commit wrongdoing; previous heads of selection such as Zhou Ji had guarded the inner and outer [offices] tightly, yet still could not prohibit it.
translations.idiomatic: The bureau clerks habitually traded favors for illicit gain. Previous directors of selection, such as Zhou Ji, had sealed the office inside and out, yet still could not stop it.

sentences.zh: 至晦，悉除之，示無防限，然處事精明，私相屬諉，罪輒得，皆以為神。

translations.literal: When it came to Hui, he removed them all, showing no defensive restrictions; yet in handling affairs he was keen and sharp—when private requests were made to entrust [appointments], guilt was immediately obtained, and all considered it miraculous.
translations.idiomatic: Hui dismissed them all and appeared to impose no restrictions at all. Yet he handled matters with such precision that whenever anyone tried to solicit a favor in private, the offense was immediately uncovered. Everyone regarded him as uncanny.

sentences.zh: 始，晦革舊示簡，廷議恐必敗，既而贓賕路塞，而流品有敘，眾乃伏。

translations.literal: At first, when Hui reformed the old ways and showed leniency, court discussion feared he would surely fail; afterward bribery and illicit gifts were blocked, and the flow of grades had order—the multitude then submitted.
translations.idiomatic: At first, when Hui reformed the old system and appeared lenient, court opinion feared he would fail. Yet bribery was soon cut off, appointments were made in proper order, and everyone submitted to his judgment.

sentences.zh: 皎被放，晦亦左除宗正卿。

translations.literal: When Jiao was released [from office], Hui was also demoted to the left as Director of the Imperial Clan.
translations.idiomatic: When Jiao was dismissed, Hui was also demoted to director of the imperial clan.

sentences.zh: 貶春州司馬，徙海州刺史，卒。

translations.literal: He was demoted to Military Adjutant of Chun Prefecture, transferred to Governor of Hai Prefecture, and died.
translations.idiomatic: He was demoted to military adjutant of Chun Prefecture, then transferred to governor of Hai Prefecture, where he died.

sentences.zh: 崔善為，貝州武城人。

translations.literal: Cui Shanwei was a native of Wucheng in Bei Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Shanwei was a native of Wucheng in Beizhou.

sentences.zh: 祖颙，為魏散騎侍郎。

translations.literal: His grandfather Yong served the Wei as Attendant Cavalier.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Yong served the Northern Wei as attendant cavalier.

sentences.zh: 善為巧於歷數，仕隋，調文林郎。

translations.literal: Shanwei was skilled in calendrical reckoning; he served the Sui and was transferred to Gentleman of the Forest of Literature.
translations.idiomatic: Shanwei was skilled in calendrical science. He served the Sui and was appointed gentleman of the forest of literature.

sentences.zh: 督工徒五百營仁壽宮，總監楊素索簿閱實，善為執板暗唱，無一差謬，素大驚。

translations.literal: He supervised five hundred laborers in building Renshou Palace; the overall supervisor Yang Su demanded the ledgers to examine the facts; Shanwei held the tally board and recited from memory in the dark—there was not one error—and Su was greatly astonished.
translations.idiomatic: He supervised five hundred laborers building Renshou Palace. When the chief supervisor Yang Su demanded the account books for inspection, Shanwei held the tally board and recited every entry from memory without a single error. Yang Su was astonished.

sentences.zh: 自是四方有疑獄，悉令按訊，皆究其情。

translations.literal: From this time on, wherever in the four directions there were doubtful legal cases, all were ordered to be investigated and examined, and in every case the facts were pursued to the end.
translations.idiomatic: From then on, whenever a doubtful case arose anywhere in the realm, he was ordered to investigate it, and he always traced the matter to its root.

sentences.zh: 仁壽中，遷樓煩司戶書佐，高祖為太守，尤禮接。

translations.literal: In the Renshou era he was transferred to Clerk of the Household Registry of Loufan; the Founding Emperor was then prefect and treated him with especial courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: During the Renshou era he was made clerk of the household registry in Loufan. The future emperor was then prefect there and treated him with exceptional courtesy.

sentences.zh: 善為見隋政日紊，密勸高祖圖天下。

translations.literal: Shanwei saw Sui government daily growing chaotic and secretly urged the Founding Emperor to plan for the realm under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing the Sui regime grow daily more corrupt, Shanwei secretly urged the future emperor to seize the empire.

sentences.zh: 及兵起，署大將軍府司戶參軍，封清河縣公。

translations.literal: When the army was raised, he was appointed Staff Administrator of the Household in the Grand General's headquarters and enfeoffed as Duke of Qinghe County.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebellion began he was made staff administrator of the household on the grand general's staff and enfeoffed as Duke of Qinghe.

sentences.zh: 擢累尚書左丞，用清察稱。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and was known for clarity and scrutiny in office.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through several posts to left vice director of the Department of State Affairs, famed for his rigorous, clear-eyed administration.

sentences.zh: 諸曹史惡之，以其短而傴，嘲曰：「曲如鉤，例封侯。」

translations.literal: The clerks of the various bureaus hated him; because he was short and hunchbacked they mocked him, saying, "Crooked as a hook—yet by precedent enfeoffed as marquis.
translations.idiomatic: The bureau clerks disliked him and mocked his short, hunched frame with the jingle, "Bent like a hook—still gets a marquis's look.

sentences.zh: 欲沮罷所任。

translations.literal: They wished to discourage and end his appointment.
translations.idiomatic: They hoped to drive him from office.

sentences.zh: 帝聞，勉之曰：「昔齊末奸吏歌斛律明月，而高緯暗不察，至滅其家。

translations.literal: The emperor heard and encouraged him, saying, "In the past at the end of Qi, corrupt clerks sang songs against Hulu Guang and the Moon; Gao Wei was dim and did not perceive it, until their families were destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor heard and consoled him, saying, "At the end of Northern Qi, corrupt officials slandered the general Hulu Guang while Emperor Gao Wei failed to see through it—and the loyal man's house was destroyed.

sentences.zh: 朕雖不德，幸免是。」

translations.literal: Though I lack virtue, I have fortunately escaped that.
translations.idiomatic: I may lack their virtue, but at least I am not blind to such slander.

sentences.zh: 因下令購謗者，謗乃止。

translations.literal: He therefore ordered a reward for the slanderers, and the slander ceased.
translations.idiomatic: He then offered a reward for informers against the mockers, and the ridicule stopped.

sentences.zh: 傅仁均撰《戊寅歷》，李淳風詆其疏，帝令善為考二家得失，多所裁正。

translations.literal: Fu Renjun compiled the Wuyin Calendar; Li Chunfeng criticized its looseness; the emperor ordered Shanwei to examine the strengths and weaknesses of both schools and made many corrections.
translations.idiomatic: When Fu Renjun compiled the Wuyin Calendar and Li Chunfeng attacked its flaws, the emperor had Shanwei compare both systems and corrected many errors.

sentences.zh: 貞觀初，為陜州刺史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhenguan he was prefect of Shaanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Zhenguan he served as prefect of Shaanzhou.

sentences.zh: 時議，戶猥地狹者徙寬鄉，善為奏：「畿內戶眾，而丁壯悉籍府兵，若聽徙，皆在關東，虛近實遠，非經通計。」

translations.literal: At the time it was debated that households in crowded places with narrow land should be moved to spacious districts; Shanwei memorialized, "Within the metropolitan region households are numerous, and all able-bodied men are registered as militia—if relocation is permitted, all will be east of the passes, emptying the near and filling the far; this is not a plan that accords with enduring principle.
translations.idiomatic: The court was debating relocating families from overcrowded districts; Shanwei argued, "The capital region is densely settled and its men are all registered as militia—moving them east of the passes would hollow out our defenses. That is unsound policy.

sentences.zh: 詔可。

translations.literal: An edict approved this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved his memorial.

sentences.zh: 歷大理、司農二卿，坐與少卿不平，出為秦州刺史。

translations.literal: He served as Minister of Justice and Minister of Agriculture in succession; because of discord with a vice minister he was sent out as prefect of Qinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He served as minister of justice and minister of agriculture; after a dispute with a vice minister he was sent out as prefect of Qinzhou.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈刑部尚書，謚曰忠。

translations.literal: He died; posthumously he was made Minister of Justice, posthumous title Zhong.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously made minister of justice with the posthumous name Zhong (Loyal).

sentences.zh: 初，天下既定，群臣居喪者皆奪服，善為建言其敝。

translations.literal: In the beginning, once the realm was settled, all ministers in mourning had their mourning garments stripped away; Shanwei memorialized on the harm of this practice.
translations.idiomatic: When the empire was first pacified, ministers in mourning were forced back to office; Shanwei memorialized against the practice.

sentences.zh: 武德二年，始許終喪，然猶時以權迫不能免，如房玄齡、褚遂良者眾矣。

translations.literal: In the second year of Wude, full mourning was first permitted, yet from time to time men were still compelled by power and could not escape it—such as Fang Xuanling and Chu Suiliang were many.
translations.idiomatic: In 619 full mourning was finally allowed, yet many were still pressed back to duty by political necessity, among them Fang Xuanling and Chu Suiliang.

sentences.zh: 李嗣真，字承胄，趙州柏人人。

translations.literal: Li Sizhen, courtesy name Chenghou, was a man of Bo in Zhao Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Li Sizhen, courtesy name Chenghou, came from Bo in Zhao Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 多藝數，舉明經，中之，累調許州司功參軍。

translations.literal: He was skilled in many arts and calculations; he presented himself for the Mingjing examination, passed, and was repeatedly transferred to Staff Administrator of Merit in Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Skilled in many arts and in calculation, he passed the Mingjing examination and served repeatedly as staff administrator of merit in Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 賀蘭敏之修撰東臺，表嗣真直弘文館，與學士劉獻臣、徐昭皆少有名，號「三少」。

translations.literal: When Helan Minzhi compiled works for the Eastern Terrace, he recommended Sizhen for duty at the Hongwen Academy; together with academicians Liu Xianchen and Xu Zhao they were all famed in youth and styled the "Three Young Men."
translations.idiomatic: When Helan Minzhi directed compilation at the Eastern Terrace he recommended Sizhen for the Hongwen Academy; Sizhen, Liu Xianchen, and Xu Zhao were famed young scholars known as the Three Young Men.

sentences.zh: 高宗東封還，詔贈孔子太師，命有司為祝，司文郎中雷少潁文不稱旨，更命嗣真，成不淹頃，帝覽稱善，詔加兩階。

translations.literal: When Gaozong returned from the eastern feng sacrifice, an edict posthumously made Confucius Grand Preceptor and ordered the relevant offices to compose a prayer; Lang of the Secretariat for Documents Lei Shaoying's text did not suit the intent, and Sizhen was ordered instead; he finished in no more than a moment; the emperor on reading praised it and ordered two ranks added.
translations.idiomatic: After Gaozong's return from the eastern feng rites, the court posthumously honored Confucius as grand preceptor and ordered a prayer composed; Lei Shaoying's draft failed to please, so Sizhen was assigned the task and finished almost instantly; the emperor praised it and promoted him two ranks.

sentences.zh: 敏之等倚恩自如，嗣真不喜，求補義烏令。

translations.literal: Minzhi and others relied on favor as they pleased; Sizhen disliked this and requested appointment as magistrate of Yiwu.
translations.idiomatic: Minzhi and his circle abused imperial favor; disliking them, Sizhen asked to be made magistrate of Yiwu.

sentences.zh: 敏之敗，學士多連坐，嗣真獨免。

translations.literal: When Minzhi fell, many academicians were implicated together; Sizhen alone escaped.
translations.idiomatic: When Minzhi fell, many academicians were punished with him; Sizhen alone was spared.

sentences.zh: 調露中，為始平令，風化大行。

translations.literal: In the Tiaolu era he was magistrate of Shiping, and moral transformation was greatly carried out.
translations.idiomatic: During Tiaolu he was magistrate of Shiping, where he won renown for transforming local customs.

sentences.zh: 時章懷太子作《寶慶曲》，閱於太清觀，嗣真謂道人劉概、輔儼曰：「宮不召商，君臣乖也；

translations.literal: At the time Crown Prince Zhanghuai composed the "Baojing Melody," which was reviewed at the Taiqing Abbey; Sizhen said to the Daoist priests Liu Kai and Fu Yan, "The palace mode does not summon the shang note—lord and minister are at odds;
translations.idiomatic: When Crown Prince Zhanghuai composed the Baojing Melody and it was performed at Taiqing Abbey, Sizhen told the Daoist priests Liu Kai and Fu Yan, "The palace mode never calls on shang—that means ruler and minister are estranged;

sentences.zh: 角與徵戾，父子疑也。

translations.literal: the jue and zhi notes clash—father and son are suspicious of each other.
translations.idiomatic: jue and zhi clash—that means father and son are at odds.

sentences.zh: 死聲多且哀，若國家無事，太子任其咎。」

translations.literal: There are many dying tones and they are mournful—if the state has no trouble, the crown prince will bear the blame.
translations.idiomatic: There are too many dying tones and they are mournful—if the realm stays quiet, the crown prince will pay for this.

sentences.zh: 俄而太子廢，概等奏其言，擢太常丞，知五禮儀，封常山縣子。

translations.literal: Before long the crown prince was deposed; Kai and others reported his words; he was promoted to Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, placed in charge of the five rites, and enfeoffed as Viscount of Changshan.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the crown prince was deposed; Kai reported Sizhen's prophecy; he was promoted to vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, put in charge of the five rites, and enfeoffed as Viscount of Changshan.

sentences.zh: 嗣真常曰：「隋樂府有《堂堂曲》，明唐再受命，比日有『側堂堂，橈堂堂』之謠，側，不正也，橈，危也。

translations.literal: Sizhen often said, "The Sui Music Bureau had the 'Tangtang Melody,' showing that Tang received the mandate anew; recently there is the ballad 'sideways tangtang, leaning tangtang'—sideways means not upright, leaning means peril.
translations.idiomatic: Sizhen often said, "The Sui court had a Tangtang melody heralding Tang's mandate; lately people sing 'sideways tangtang, tilting tangtang'—sideways means crooked rule, tilting means danger.

sentences.zh: 皇帝病日侵，事皆決中宮，持權與人，收之不易。

translations.literal: The emperor's illness daily worsens; all affairs are decided in the inner palace; once power is given to others, it is not easily taken back.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor grows sicker daily; the inner palace decides everything; once power is handed out, it is hard to reclaim.

sentences.zh: 宗室雖眾，居中制外，勢且不敵。

translations.literal: Though the imperial clan is numerous, holding the center and controlling the outside, in strength they cannot match.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial clan is numerous, but those who hold the center control the periphery—they cannot prevail.

sentences.zh: 諸王殆為後所蹂踐，吾見難作不久矣。」

translations.literal: The princes will likely be trampled by what follows—I see trouble arising before long.
translations.idiomatic: The princes will be crushed in what comes—I see calamity approaching soon.

sentences.zh: 太常缺黃鐘，鑄不能成，嗣真居崇業裏，疑土中有之，弗得其所。

translations.literal: The Court of Imperial Sacrifices lacked a huangzhong bell; casting could not succeed. Sizhen lived in Chongye Lane and suspected one lay in the earth but could not find its place.
translations.idiomatic: The Court of Imperial Sacrifices lacked a huangzhong bell and could not cast one; living in Chongye Lane, Sizhen suspected the bell lay buried nearby but could not locate it.

sentences.zh: 道上逢一車，有鐸聲甚厲，嗣真曰：「宮聲也。」

translations.literal: On the road he met a cart with a very sharp bell-clapper sound; Sizhen said, "That is the palace tone.
translations.idiomatic: On the road he heard a cart bell ring sharply and said, "That is the palace tone.

sentences.zh: 市以歸，振於空地，若有應者，掘之得鐘，眾樂遂和。

translations.literal: He bought it and returned home, struck it in an open place, and as if in response dug and obtained the bell; all the music was thereby harmonized.
translations.idiomatic: He bought the bell, struck it in an open field, dug where it resonated, and unearthed the huangzhong; thereafter the court music was in tune.

sentences.zh: 嘗引工展器於廷，後奇其風度應對，召相王府參軍閻玄靜圖之，吏部郎中楊誌誠為贊，秘書郎殷仲容書，時以為寵。

translations.literal: Once he led craftsmen to display instruments in court; the empress was struck by his bearing and replies, summoned Yan Xuanjing of the Prince of Xiang's staff to paint his portrait, had Director in the Ministry of Personnel Yang Zhicheng compose an encomium and Secretary Yin Zhongrong write it—at the time this was considered great favor.
translations.idiomatic: Once he displayed instruments for the court; the empress admired his bearing and had Yan Xuanjing paint his portrait, with an encomium by Yang Zhicheng and calligraphy by Yin Zhongrong—a mark of special favor.

sentences.zh: 永昌初，以右御史中丞知大夫事，請周、漢為二王後，詔可。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yongchang he served as Right Vice Censor-in-Chief acting in censor-in-chief affairs, requested that Zhou and Han be made successors to the Two Kings, and an edict approved this.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Yongchang he served as right vice censor-in-chief in charge of censorate affairs, petitioned to restore the Zhou and Han as ritual successors to the Two Kings, and the edict was approved.

sentences.zh: 命巡撫河東，薦宋溫瑾、袁嘉祚、李日知，拔州縣職，皆至顯官。

translations.literal: He was ordered to tour and comfort Hedong, recommended Song Wenjin, Yuan Jiazuo, and Li Rizhi, and promoted men from prefectural and county posts—all reached eminent office.
translations.idiomatic: Ordered to tour Hedong, he recommended Song Wenjin, Yuan Jiazuo, and Li Rizhi, elevating local officials who all rose to high office.

sentences.zh: 來俊臣獄方熾，嗣真上書諫，以為「昔陳平事漢祖，謀疏楚君臣，行反間，項羽遂亡。

translations.literal: When Lai Junchen's prison prosecutions were blazing, Sizhen submitted a memorial remonstrating, saying, "In the past Chen Ping served Han Zu, plotted to separate Chu lord and ministers, carried out counter-intelligence, and Xiang Yu was thereby destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: As Lai Junchen's purges raged, Sizhen memorialized, "Chen Ping once served Han Gaozu by sowing discord among Xiang Yu's followers until Chu collapsed.

sentences.zh: 今殆有如平者謀陛下君臣，恐為社稷禍」。

translations.literal: Now there is likely someone like Ping plotting against Your Majesty's lord-and-minister bond—I fear calamity for the altars of state."
translations.idiomatic: Someone like Chen Ping may now be driving a wedge between Your Majesty and your ministers—I fear disaster for the realm."

sentences.zh: 不納。

translations.literal: This was not accepted.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was ignored.

sentences.zh: 出為潞州刺史。

translations.literal: He was sent out as prefect of Luzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as prefect of Luzhou.

sentences.zh: 俊臣誣以反，流藤州，久得還。

translations.literal: Junchen falsely accused him of rebellion and he was banished to Tengzhou; after a long time he was able to return.
translations.idiomatic: Junchen framed him for treason and exiled him to Tengzhou; years later he was allowed to return.

sentences.zh: 自筮死日，豫具棺斂，如言卒桂陽。

translations.literal: He divined his own death day, prepared coffin and shroud in advance, and died at Guiyang as foretold.
translations.idiomatic: He divined the day of his death, prepared his coffin in advance, and died at Guiyang exactly as predicted.

sentences.zh: 有詔州縣護喪還鄉里，贈濟州刺史，謚曰昭。

translations.literal: An edict ordered prefectures and counties to escort the funeral back to his home district; posthumously he was made Governor of Jizhou, posthumous title Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered his remains escorted home, posthumously made him governor of Jizhou, and gave him the posthumous name Zhao.

sentences.zh: 武後嘗問嗣真儲貳事，對曰：「程嬰、杵臼存趙氏孤，古人嘉之。」

translations.literal: Empress Wu once asked Sizhen about the heir apparent; he replied, "Cheng Ying and Gongsun Chujiu preserved the orphan of Zhao—the ancients praised this.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wu once asked him about the heir apparent; he answered, "Cheng Ying and Gongsun Chujiu saved the Zhao orphan—the ancients praised them for it.

sentences.zh: 後悟，中宗乃安。

translations.literal: Later she understood, and Zhongzong was thereby secured.
translations.idiomatic: She later understood his meaning, and Zhongzong's position was secured.

sentences.zh: 神龍初，贈御史大夫。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Shenlong he was posthumously made Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Shenlong he was posthumously made censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 所撰述尤多。

translations.literal: His writings and compositions were especially numerous.
translations.idiomatic: He left a large body of writings.

sentences.zh: 時雍州人裴知古亦善樂律，長安中，為太樂令。

translations.literal: At the time Pei Zhigu of Yong Prefecture was also skilled in musical pitch laws; in Chang'an he served as Director of the Grand Music Office.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Pei Zhigu of Yong Prefecture was also skilled in music theory and served in Chang'an as director of the Grand Music Office.

sentences.zh: 神龍元年正月，享太廟，樂作，知古密語萬年令元行沖曰：「金石諧婉，將有大慶，在唐室子孫乎！」

translations.literal: In the first month of the first year of Shenlong, when the imperial ancestors were honored in the Grand Temple and music was performed, Zhigu whispered to Yuan Xingchong, magistrate of Wannian, "Metal and stone are harmonious and gentle—there will be a great celebration; will it be among the descendants of the House of Tang?
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of Shenlong 1, during the ancestral rites at the Grand Temple, Zhigu whispered to Wannian magistrate Yuan Xingchong, "The bells and chimes sound harmonious—a great joy is coming; will it fall to Tang's own descendants?

sentences.zh: 是月，中宗復位。

translations.literal: That month Zhongzong was restored to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: That same month Zhongzong was restored to the throne.

sentences.zh: 人有乘馬者，知古聞其嘶，乃曰：「馬鳴哀，主必墜死。」

translations.literal: When someone was riding a horse, Zhigu heard its neigh and said, "The horse's cry is mournful—the rider will surely fall and die.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing a rider's horse neigh mournfully, he said, "That cry is a death omen—the rider will fall and die.

sentences.zh: 見新婚者，聞佩聲，曰：「終必離。」

translations.literal: Seeing newlyweds, he heard the sound of their girdle pendants and said, "In the end they will surely part."
translations.idiomatic: Passing newlyweds, he heard their pendants chime and said, "They will not stay together."

sentences.zh: 訪之，皆然。

translations.literal: On inquiry, in every case it was so.
translations.idiomatic: In every case inquiry proved him right.
